This study introduces a method for real-time, interactive highlighting of relevant anatomical structures during intraoperative navigation in eye surgery. The approach utilizes a depth camera to detect the surgical device and tracks it alongside a patient-specific 3D model of relevant anatomy. By calculating the device's position relative to key anatomical features, the system projects dynamic highlights onto the device's image within a live video feed. This capability allows surgeons to interactively emphasize critical structures in real time. The method's efficacy was validated using video footage from two retinal surgeries.

We demonstrate that the $F$-functions defined by the integral $\int_0^1 x^{\alpha-1} (1-x)^{\beta-1} K_\mu(\sqrt{abx(1-x)}) dx$ satisfy a pair of second-order differential equations. Each equation involves $F$-functions with arguments $ax(1-x)$ and $abx(1-x)$, respectively. These results are instrumental in deriving expressions for $F$-functions featuring arguments of the form $a(bx+c)(dx+e)$.

This paper examines the viability of a passwordless verification system based on FIDO2 within the current digital landscape. It investigates the feasibility of deploying FIDO2 across all devices, specifically focusing on the technical and economic hurdles faced by low-end hardware. Additionally, the paper analyzes the impact of widespread adoption on existing security and privacy protocols, while also addressing the broader social and ethical ramifications of this shift.

This note examines the Weyl-Wigner framework for analyzing lattice systems, a structure characterized by configurations of particles with periodic boundary conditions. We demonstrate that within the semi-classical regime, the Weyl-Wigner distribution for these systems can be expressed as a summation of Weyl-Wigner distributions corresponding to the torus. This decomposition facilitates the derivation of an evolution equation for the Weyl-Wigner distribution, which displays a novel form.

The architecture of online platforms significantly influences user behavior. This study examines how YouTube's structural design impacts user autonomy. Specifically, it analyzes the correlation between platform features and the degree of user engagement, as well as the link between the social hierarchy formed by view counts and the perceived control users have over their own engagement. The findings indicate that YouTube's hierarchical structure reinforces existing disparities in popularity, exacerbating the "Matthew Effect" (where the rich get richer). Additionally, the platform's algorithmic sorting and recommendation systems substantially diminish users' ability to manage their own engagement levels.

This study demonstrates the practical completeness of the $\pi$-calculus, defined as every process admitting at least one name-guaranteed sequence of transitions that inevitably reaches a state where no further transitions are possible, termed a "deadlock." This result relies on a novel, computable notion of equivalence for the deadlock class, which is proven to possess finite orbits under the $\pi$-calculus' transition system. Consequently, the paper establishes that determining whether a process belongs to this class is a decidable problem.

This paper introduces a method to generate the Hamiltonian path within the graph of labeled binary trees, where each successive tree in each sequence differs from its predecessor in exactly one parent-child relationship. This "gray code" of structured trees is constructed by applying a similar path to the Gray code of hypercubes, where successive integers in each dimension differ from their neighbors by only a single bit in binary representation. This study also examines the connection between these two types of Gray codes.

The sPHENIX experiment, currently under construction at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC), is designed to investigate the properties of the strongly-coupled quark-gluon plasma (QGP) formed during heavy-ion collisions. It also aims to conduct precision measurements of high-transverse-momentum (high-pT) hadrons and jets in proton-proton (pp) collisions to validate the perturbative QCD framework. A key component of this analysis is reconstructing high-pT jets and individual hadrons using the reconstructed charged-particle tracks provided by the experiment's silicon tracker. This paper outlines the implementation of the Automated Combinatorial Track Selection (ACTS) algorithm within the sPHENIX software framework. The study evaluates the algorithm's track-finding performance in pp data and reports on its application in the Pb+Pb dataset. Furthermore, it details the algorithm's adaptation for use in sPHENIX's Time Projection Chamber (TPC) during heavy-ion collisions.

The space-time finite element method (FETD) is a prominent numerical technique for solving hyperbolic partial differential equations (PDEs) featuring internal interfaces, such as moving discontinuities. A critical component of FETD is the "jump term," which represents the temporal discretization of the weak form's jump conditions at these interfaces. This paper introduces a new FETD framework that supports arbitrary temporal degrees of freedom (DOFs), including discontinuous Galerkin (DG) and continuous Galerkin (Cg) methods. We establish the jump-term formula for both approaches and demonstrate that the discontinuous FETD-GD variant achieves second-order accuracy, whereas the continuous FETD-CG variant reaches third-order accuracy. Furthermore, we provide a theoretical proof demonstrating that FETD-GD maintains second-order accuracy and FETD-CG maintains third-order accuracy in the presence of moving discontinuities. We also present a numerical example to validate these theoretical findings.

This paper examines circular flows within signed networks, adhering to a specific constraint: each edge must carry equal but opposite integer values depending on its orientation (+1 or -1). We introduce a novel mono-directional signed network framework, where all edges share the same orientation, to analyze the minimum capacity required for existence of circular currents satisfying this constraint. The discussion outlines the necessary and sufficient conditions defining such networks as "mono-directed signed network," which possess feasible circular currents under these specific constraints. The paper also presents a constructive algorithm to generate these circular flows within mono-directed signed networks. The paper concludes by demonstrating the equivalence between circular flows within these mono-directed signed networks and standard flows within unsigned networks.

The Modular Subset Total problem involves finding a subset of rows from a matrix that sum to a target vector modulo $k$. This challenge is widely regarded as computationally difficult, with the best-known algorithms running in $O(2^{k/2+o(k)})$ time for the case where $k$ is fixed. In this work, we introduce an improved algorithm that achieves $O(2^{k/3+o(k)})$ runtime. Our approach relies on a divide-and-conquer strategy that splits the target vector into three parts, solving each recursively and then merging the partial results. Crucially, we demonstrate that the method for combining these partitions can be executed deterministically in a time proportional to the sum of the squares of the individual partition times, thereby enabling a straightforward runtime analysis.

This study introduces a novel catalog of M-dwarf outbursts identified by the All-Sky Automated Survey for Supernova (ASAS-SN). The catalog encompasses 1,000 outbursts from 300 M-dwarf stars, with 200 stars having previously unpublished events. The majority of these objects are M3 to M5 spectral types, exhibiting peak brightnesses between $V = 10.5$ and $14.5$ mag. The catalog details the coordinates, magnitudes, and timing of each event, alongside derived outburst parameters such as rise and fall durations, full width at half maximum (FWHM), and full width at tenth maximum (FWTM). The authors also present a statistical analysis of the catalog's properties, including the distribution of outburst recurrence intervals, peak magnitudes, and characteristic timescales. The paper concludes with a discussion on the physical mechanisms driving these events.

This study introduces a new approach to semi-supervised speech identification (SSID) that leverages a comparative Siamese network (CSN) to enhance the performance of limited labeled data. The CSN processes a pair of speech utterances, one labeled and one unlabeled, to generate a corresponding label prediction. The model is trained by maximizing the agreement between this prediction and the actual ground truth of the unlabeled input. Experimental results demonstrate that this proposed method surpasses existing state-of-the-art SSID techniques.

This study examines the axial and vector framework functions within the context of charged and neutral lepton-nucleon scattering. It is demonstrated that the axial structure function $b_1$ is directly linked to the twist-2 twist-3 $g_1$ and $g_2$ generalized parton distributions, whereas the vector structure function $f_1$ is expressed through twist-2 $F_2$ and $F_L$ and twist-3 $f_L$ and $f_L$ transverse structure functions. These relationships are analyzed regarding their scaling behavior, and it is observed that $f_1$ and $b_1$ are anticipated to be negligible at small Bjorken-$x$ and large $Q^2$. Furthermore, the potential for extracting $f_1$ and $b_1$ from experimental charged and neutral lepton-nucleon scattering data is evaluated.

This study addresses the nearly certain stabilization of adaptive linear-quadratic control systems characterized by a hidden Markov chain across an infinite timeline. The primary objective is to determine an optimal policy that minimizes the expected discounted cost while ensuring the probability of system instability approaches zero. The proposed solution involves a two-stage methodology: first, a model-based adaptive policy is established for a predefined infinite-horizon model, and second, an adaptive policy is constructed for the actual system utilizing model-based feedback. The paper examines the necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of such policies, along with their derivation. Furthermore, it establishes a theorem proving that the model-based policy effectively stabilizes the true system with near-certainty, supported by numerical examples.

The brain's ability to process and integrate information from diverse sources is essential for perception and action. This paper introduces a new multi-modal and multi-factor branch-based temporal active inference framework, extending the principles of free energy minimization. This enhanced model supports the generation of multiple branching pathways for multi-factor temporal inference and handles data from various modalities. We demonstrate the model's efficacy through two case studies: first, a multi-modal, multi-factor temporal active inference system for brain-computer interfaces, and second, a multi-factor temporal active inference architecture for brain-machine integration.

This study examines the behavior of KdV solitons within a frigid quark-gluon plasma, specifically within the framework of the low-energy effective theory of QCD. We demonstrate that the KdV equation governing the solitons is derived from the energy-momentum tensor of this QCD effective theory. Furthermore, we analyze the influence of temperature on soliton mass and width, alongside an investigation into the effects of viscosity on the solitons' propagation dynamics.

We establish that for any Banach space $X$, the property of the associated locally convex $\epsilon$-space being Eberlein-Grothendieck is equivalent to its completeness, where $\epsilon$ denotes the weak* topology on the dual of $X$ and Eberlein-Grothendieck refers to compactness in this topology. Furthermore, we demonstrate that for any locally $\epsilon$-F-space, being Eberlein-Grothendieck is equivalent to being a Banach space.

The authors show that these signature curves facilitate the identification of periodic orbits and enable the construction of new ones. Furthermore, the study reveals that distinct initial conditions yield signature curves with unique patterns, allowing for the classification of orbits based on their shapes. Ultimately, the research highlights the potential of similarity signatures as a robust analytical tool for both detecting and designing periodic trajectories in chaotic systems.

This study examines the properties of the LAN (local asymptotic normality) for parameter families arising from solutions to stochastic differential equations driven by Lé processes. Specifically, we demonstrate that the Hida white noise $L^2$-version of the Kallenberg density function associated with these solutions possesses LAN features. Additionally, the paper establishes the optimality of parametric inference procedures for this broad category of equations. Our work advances existing literature by demonstrating that the requisite local asymptotic normality can be established within the framework of Hida white noise $L^2$, thereby allowing for the derivation of optimal estimation rates in scenarios where traditional methods encounter difficulties.

This study examines the twisted Laplacian on Riemannian manifolds, particularly the hyperbolic case, by analyzing the Teichmüller representation derived from a conformal mapping. By establishing a relationship between the twisted Laplacian and the Laplace-Beltrami operator, we determine the spectrum of the twisted Laplacian for a specific class of functions, which is also linked to the theory of Hilbert spaces of analytic functions.

This study investigates the generalized phantom traveler dark energy (GGPDE) framework within Saez-Ballester gravitational theory. Furthermore, we evaluate the model's consistency with observational data, including the Hubble diagram of Type Ia supernovae, baryon acoustic oscillations, and the cosmic microwave background. Our results indicate that the GGPDE model aligns well with current cosmological observations.

This study examines a competition among multiple edge servers, each with distinct processing capabilities, to fulfill user service requests. A user may delegate a request to various servers, which are tasked with executing a sequence of operations. We model this scenario as a Markov decision process (MDP) to determine the optimal task-chaining strategy for users, aiming to minimize the sum of processing delays and monetary costs. Simultaneously, we introduce a game-theoretic framework to derive optimal pricing strategies for the servers. We demonstrate that the pricing game possesses a unique pure-strategy Nash equilibrium. Furthermore, we propose a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) approach to approximate the users' optimal task-chaining policies. Simulation results indicate that the DRL-based strategy significantly outperforms existing methods, yielding substantial improvements in both task completion rates and server profits.

Depression is a pervasive mental health condition affecting millions globally, characterized by persistent sadness, loss of interest, and diminished self-worth. While much research has been dedicated to the negative aspects of this disorder, the joy individuals experience during life often goes unnoticed. This study examines the positive moments reported by individuals living with depression, utilizing a dataset of 1,000+ user-generated narratives from the Depression Online Forum. The analysis reveals that these individuals frequently articulate joy and hope, identifying specific triggers such as personal growth, meaningful relationships, and spiritual or religious practices. Furthermore, the findings indicate that users with chronic depression are more prone to recalling happy events than those with a single episode. The paper concludes by discussing the significance of these insights for both clinical practice and the broader public.

This work investigates the isospin disruption transition within the SU(2) gauge theory of two flavors, employing an Sp(4) gauge theory that includes identical quark masses as a surrogate model. By utilizing lattice Monte Carlo simulations, we demonstrate that the isospin disruption transition in the Sp(4) framework remains robust against finite-volume effects, even more so than the corresponding transition in the original SU(2) theory. Consequently, the Sp(4) model offers a viable and reliable framework for determining the critical temperature associated with isospin disruption in the SU(2) theory.

We introduce a novel tellurite compound, $\text{Na}_{4-\delta}\text{NiTeO}_6$ (where $\delta \approx 0.1$), which features a zigzag magnetic configuration. This material is characterized by a tetragonal structure with a $P4/mmm$ space group, containing two distinct Na sites and a deficiency in Na content. The Ni$^{2+}$ ions, possessing a $d^{10}$ electronic configuration, form linear chains within the $ab$-plane, creating a one-dimensional triangular lattice. Magnetic susceptibility data reveal a peak at $T_{\text{max}} = 10.5$ K, corresponding to the Néel temperature ($T_N$). The observed zigzag magnetic arrangement arises from competing exchange interactions between nearest-neighbor ($J_1$) and next-nearest-neighbor ($J_2$) triangular sites. Additionally, the magnetization behavior under varying magnetic fields and temperature indicates a significant transverse anisotropy, attributed to the specific crystallographic orientation of the Ni$^{2+}$ ions.

The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into the Internet of Things (IoT) has catalyzed the development of intelligent vehicular networks (IVN), which promise to revolutionize transportation by enhancing safety, efficiency, and sustainability. However, the widespread adoption of AI-driven IVN faces significant hurdles, primarily stemming from the inherent unpredictability of AI algorithms and the absence of a defined trust framework. This study introduces a theoretical architecture for trust governance within IVN environments characterized by uncertainty. By conceptualizing trust as a mechanism to manage the risks associated with AI unpredictability, the research establishes a formal framework for the IVN environment. This framework delineates the necessary components for implementing a robust trust governance structure, specifically focusing on trust measurement, assessment, and the establishment of trust. Furthermore, the study employs a game-theoretic approach to model the interactions between AI agents and the trust governance system, demonstrating that this structure can effectively mitigate risks arising from AI unpredictability. Ultimately, the paper argues that implementing such a trust governance structure is essential for facilitating the secure and reliable deployment of AI within IVN.

We examine the challenge of estimating the derivative of a function that is both monotonic and thrice differentiable, evaluated at a point where its magnitude reaches a maximum. This specific difficulty arises in the context of a single-index function estimator with known bounds on its Lipschitz continuity. We demonstrate that applying a simple cubic spline estimator, utilizing data from $n$ points, achieves a convergence rate of $O(n^{-2/3})$ in the $L_1$ norm. This rate is optimal for general functions within the specified class, provided the curvature bounds are not excessively stringent.

This paper investigates the properties of scalar field configurations within AdS-Taub-NUT spacetime, a model representing precise black bounces. We demonstrate that the AdS curvature is essential for stabilizing the scalar field's negative energy state, thereby preventing negative energy from accumulating in the Taub-NUT region. Furthermore, we analyze the behavior of the scalar field at the AdS horizon and examine the cosmic censorship conjecture regarding these precise black bounces.

This study introduces a new approach to the automatic identification of speech distortions, encompassing background noise, audio artifacts, and other signal impairments. The proposed method leverages extensive taxonomies of speech distortions to achieve superior performance compared to conventional techniques. The method's efficacy is validated through a comparison against a standard audio tagging dataset, demonstrating its robustness in handling diverse and complex distortion scenarios.

This study introduces a novel dynamic mean-field theory designed to analyze the dynamics of open systems interacting with a thermal bath. By applying this framework to a harmonic oscillator, we demonstrate that it yields results indistinguishable from those derived via the path-integral approach. Furthermore, we illustrate the framework's versatility by applying it to two distinct scenarios: a two-state molecular switch influenced by solvent fluctuations and a reaction network driven by external forces.

We present a new structure called Sentence Links to represent discourse connections. This structure explicitly models the relationships between sentences, including both local links between adjacent sentences and long-range connections spanning multiple sentences. To effectively represent these diverse links, we integrate them into our structure using a query-and-response framework. This representation method is designed to enhance the performance of downstream tasks, such as discourse tree parsing and summarization.

This paper presents a comprehensive review of the As-Layer (ASL), a two-dimensional resistive structure designed to facilitate efficient hyperbolic wave transmission. The review examines the ASL's equivalent circuit model, its electromagnetic characteristics, and its primary applications in transmitting both surface waves and leaky waves.

This study details the interaction between laser pulses and droplets, revealing that such engagement induces a phase shift within the droplet array. The laser pulse triggers a vaporization process in the droplet's center, creating a vapor cavity that subsequently expands outward. The resulting rapid movement of this vapor cavity generates a shock wave, which in turn causes the array to fragment. The magnitude of the phase shift is contingent upon the laser pulse's energy, with higher intensities producing greater shifts. The maximum propagation distance of the vapor cavity is determined by the droplet's radius, as a larger diameter facilitates greater distances for the shock wave to travel.

The Internet of Things (IoT) is a ubiquitous paradigm that connects physical objects to the Internet, enabling them to exchange data and services. However, the sheer scale of IoT devices and the resulting massive data volumes pose significant challenges for current network architectures. To address this, the Pub/Sub (Producer/Subscriber) model has emerged as a flexible solution for data orchestration, offering a decoupled architecture that facilitates efficient information sharing. This paper introduces the Pub/Sub-SDN (Software-Defined Networking) framework, which integrates the Pub/Sub model with SDN to create a scalable, flexible, and efficient orchestration architecture. By leveraging the control plane separation inherent in SDN, this framework enables dynamic management of subscribers and producers, thereby optimizing data flow. The study outlines the core components of this architecture and provides a detailed analysis of its operational mechanisms.

The LkH$\alpha\,330$ system, a young T Tauri star located in the Taurus molecular cloud at a distance of 140 pc, exhibits a strong H$\alpha$ emission line, indicating the presence of an actively accreting protoplanetary disk. This study presents new observations of the disk's structure and composition, utilizing ALMA data for millimeter-wave continuum emission alongside VLT/SPHERE data for scattered light. We detect a prominent gap in the millimeter continuum at 1.2 arcseconds (corresponding to 100 astronomical units) and a corresponding gap in the scattered light at 0.3 arcseconds (30 astronomical units). Analysis of the scattered light reveals a power-law slope of $\alpha = 1.3 \pm 0.1$, suggesting a population of small grains with sizes between 0.1 and 10 micrometers. Furthermore, we observe a significant depletion of millimeter continuum emission at 1.2 arcseconds, indicating a depletion factor of 100 relative to the surrounding disk. This depletion implies a substantial reduction in the mass of millimeter-sized grains. We propose that the gap in the scattered light arises from the depletion of sub-micrometer grains, while the gap in the continuum is caused by the depletion of millimeter-sized grains. This scenario is consistent with the presence of a young planet orbiting the star.

The European Union's 2050 carbon neutrality goals necessitate the decarbonization of the energy sector, with hydrogen emerging as a critical component. This study examines the economic and environmental feasibility of a European hydrogen grid, utilizing the open-source PyPSA-Eur model to simulate a fully integrated electricity, hydrogen, and industry network. The analysis evaluates two scenarios: a baseline that maintains the current reliance on fossil fuels, and an alternative that fully integrates renewable energy sources. The results demonstrate that hydrogen is essential for meeting the 2050 climate targets, with the optimal strategy involving a fully renewable system. In this scenario, the hydrogen network achieves its maximum potential, characterized by extensive interconnectivity and a total annual production volume of 1,000 TWh.

The Cosmic Ray (CR) induced muon flux exhibits an annual variation, with the peak typically occurring in late June or early July. This phenomenon is attributed to the seasonal shift in CR intensity at Earth's upper atmosphere, combined with changes in the overlying atmospheric mass that affect muon attenuation. While the flux variation at vertical detectors is well-documented, horizontal components have received less attention. This study examines the annual variation of horizontal muon fields, focusing on the relative timing between the horizontal and vertical flux peaks. We present data from the MINERvA experiment at Fermilab, which recorded muon fluxes over a two-year period. Our results indicate that the horizontal flux peak consistently lags behind the vertical flux peak by approximately 20 to 30 days. This time difference aligns with expectations for muons traversing the Earth's surface at a shallow angle, suggesting that horizontal flux measurements can be utilized to probe subsurface density structures.

We introduce a photonic architecture designed to generate squeezed electromagnetic fields, offering the advantage of topological protection against certain perturbations. This system utilizes two coupled, L-shaped waveguides, where the waveguide junction functions as a topological insulator. Consequently, the system exhibits topological robustness regarding perturbations that maintain symmetry, specifically those that do not couple the waveguide's two polarization modes. Our analysis reveals that the system's topological characteristics can be fully described by a simplified, one-dimensional model. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the system supports squeezed illumination suitable for applications such as quantum-enhanced sensing and metrology.

This study addresses the challenge of generating smooth, duration-optimized trajectories for drones moving between two points while adhering to specific physical constraints. It begins by deriving a theoretical optimal path based on fixed time assumptions, subsequently extending this to variable time scenarios through the application of time-scaling functions. The authors demonstrate that the resulting path is not only time-optimal but also exhibits enhanced smoothness, a quality that significantly reduces mechanical stress on the vehicle. Furthermore, the paper investigates path smoothness in greater detail and proposes a novel function designed to balance the trade-off between flight duration and smoothness.

This study introduces a novel algebraic framework for classifying and analyzing additive F_q-conjucyclic codes defined over finite fields F_{q^2}. By employing a specific isomorphism, we map these codes to left ideals within a specific non-commutative polynomial ring. This transformation facilitates the derivation of structural properties for such codes, including their closure under specific operations, dimension, and cardinality. Furthermore, we establish that these codes can be represented using a generator polynomial and a set of polynomials known as the parial basis.

The report outlines the specific research questions and community needs identified through the process, alongside the corresponding recommendations. The authors also examine the current state of HEP community involvement, focusing on the roles of the broader community, its interaction with universities, and its engagement with the public. The report further highlights the importance of supporting the diverse demographics of HEP researchers, including those from underrepresented backgrounds, women, and junior scientists. This study reports an analysis of $W$ boson orientation within $t\bar{t}$ events, utilizing an ATLAS dataset from $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 8$ TeV with an integrated luminosity of 20.3 fb$^{-1}$. The investigation focuses on the lepton+jets decay channel, employing a $t\bar{t}$ sample reconstructed via a single jet and two leptons. The analysis utilizes a novel discriminant to isolate $t\bar{t}$ processes from backgrounds, achieving a signal purity of 90.5% and a signal efficiency of 30.5%. The results demonstrate that the $W$ boson's angular distribution is governed by the top quark's spin density matrix, which in turn is dictated by the production mechanism. Furthermore, the study confirms that the top quark's polarization is predominantly driven by the $q\bar{q}$ annihilation process.

By utilizing the QCD sum rules method, we investigate the sum rules for the operators $q\bar{q}q\bar{q}$, $q\bar{q}q\bar{q}q\bar{q}$, and $q\bar{q}q\bar{q}q\bar{q}q\bar{q}$, which correspond to the quark and anti-quark components of the $D$-meson. Our results indicate that the twist-3 distribution functions for the $D$-meson are significantly smaller than the twist-2 counterparts. This paper examines the exponential hypergraph, defined as a hypergraph where its vertex set corresponds to the vertices of a graph $G$ and its vertex set consists of hyperedges formed by the edges of $G$ and all their subsets. We demonstrate that the spectrum of the exponential hypergraph is determined by the spectrum of the underlying graph $G$ and its signless Laplacian. Furthermore, we establish that the exponential hypergraph is integral precisely when the underlying graph is both integral and bipartite. The study also defines signed subhyperedges as specific assignments of positive or negative signs to each hyperedge while retaining the original adjacency structure. We characterize integrality for these signed hypergraphs and prove that a signed exponential hypergraph is integral if and only if its corresponding unsigned version is integral.

The global navigation satellite system (GNSS) is a critical infrastructure supporting numerous global services, including aviation, telecommunications, and emergency response. However, the system is vulnerable to interference and cyberattacks, which can cause significant disruptions. To address this, we propose a collaborative localisation approach for the Starlink network that leverages the massive scale of its satellites to enhance global positioning accuracy. This paper introduces a new method for estimating receiver positions by utilizing multiple satellites simultaneously, thereby reducing localisation errors. We demonstrate the method's effectiveness through simulations and experiments, showing that it can significantly improve positioning precision compared to traditional techniques.

Hot Jupiters are known to undergo tidal evolution, which typically drives their orbital eccentricities toward zero and their periods toward synchronization. However, the specific evolutionary paths of these systems remain uncertain. This study analyzes transit timing data for XO-3b, a hot Jupiter with an exceptionally long period of 10.8 days, to determine its specific trajectory. By applying a transit timing variation (TTV) model, we identified a significant semi-amplitude of 1.13 ± 0.06 minutes, indicating that the planet is far from a circular orbit. Furthermore, we modeled the system's evolution using a tidal evolution framework that accounts for the planet's internal structure. Our results indicate that XO-3b is currently in a transitional state, moving from an initial eccentric state toward a synchronized spin-orbit configuration. This evolutionary path is consistent with a tidal quality factor ($Q$) of approximately $10^5$ and a rotational period of roughly 1.5 times the orbital period.

The 21-cm universal signal from neutral hydrogen is a highly promising target for future cosmological observations. However, the signal's extremely low amplitude and significant contamination from foreground sources make extracting the cosmological information challenging. Consequently, cosmologists have developed various theoretical models to describe the signal's evolution, yet these models often fail to capture the full complexity of the underlying physics. This paper introduces a Bayesian framework for calibrating the signal by fitting a model to data, accounting for both model and wavelet uncertainties. We demonstrate that this approach can effectively recover the signal's evolution, even when the underlying model is imperfect.

This work examines the relationship between the standard Gromov-Witten theory of a complex vector bundle and that of its zero-section hypersurface. We demonstrate that for any vector bundle residing on a complete smooth variety, a specific subset of the bundle's Gromov-Witten invariants can be derived from the corresponding zero-section invariants.

This article introduces a theorem establishing that the traditional Prime Number Theorem holds with uniform consistency across any given sub-interval within the domain of natural numbers, provided these subsets are not too large. This approach allows for a consistent determination of the required error margin. Furthermore, an estimated error range is provided for small values.

This paper introduces a method for modeling longitudinal data using natural cubic splines, with the objective of analyzing clinical trials for Alzheimer's disease. The approach is evaluated through both simulation and real-world data.

This paper introduces a crowdsourcing algorithm designed for autonomous vehicles to detect parking spots. The proposed method enables a fleet of self-driving cars to map parking locations by sharing sensor data, thereby reducing the burden on individual vehicles. We present a novel algorithm that selects the optimal subset of cars to physically visit each parking spot, balancing the trade-off between the total number of mapped spots and the fleet's operational costs. The algorithm is optimized to maximize the number of locations mapped while minimizing the number of cars deployed. The paper also details the design of a specialized communication protocol for these vehicles to exchange sensor data and discusses the system's implementation. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through a simulation that measures both the count of mapped parking spots and the associated algorithmic costs. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of efficiency.

This study investigates the convergence behavior of the minimizers of empirical risk functionals, which are defined as the minimum values obtained by training neural networks on finite datasets. We establish that these functionals are continuous almost surely, provided the training data is i.i.d. drawn from a uniform distribution, under the condition that the training functionals are uniformly continuous. We further demonstrate that the minimizers of empirical risk functionals are consistent estimators of the underlying population minimizers, provided certain assumptions hold. We also discuss the implications of these results for the convergence behavior of the minimizers of empirical risk functionals, which are defined as the minimum values obtained by training neural networks on finite datasets. This study introduces a reflective, parametric frequency-discriminative circuit capable of limiting RF input power to a sub-milliwatt range while maintaining an output power of approximately one microwatt. The architecture utilizes two cascaded reflective parametric frequency filters (PFFs) to achieve frequency selectivity, whereas an integrated Josephson junction (JJ) provides the limiting functionality. The PFFs are engineered to suppress unwanted frequency components, allowing only the desired signal to pass through to the limiting stage. The Josephson junction, biased with a direct current, attenuates high-power RF inputs by introducing non-linear phase shifts that disrupt the transmitted signal. Theoretical analysis and experimental results confirm that the proposed system achieves a frequency rejection ratio exceeding 20 dB between adjacent channels and a dynamic range of 30 dB across limiting thresholds. The system operates with a minimum power requirement of approximately 1 microwatt, making it highly energy-efficient. The Josephson junction is fabricated using standard superconducting niobium technology, ensuring compatibility with existing quantum computing and communication infrastructure. The reflective configuration offers several advantages, including reduced size, lower insertion loss, and improved isolation between input and output ports. The system's performance is validated through rigorous testing, demonstrating its potential for applications in high-frequency communication systems, radar, and quantum computing environments. This study examines the epidemic progression of SARS-CoV-2 under the assumption of zero acquired immunity, utilizing a comprehensive SEIRS framework. The model incorporates the latent period, symptomatic and asymptomatic infection pathways, and the impacts of social distancing and lockdowns. Additionally, it accounts for the natural and policy-driven effects of social distancing on transmission rates. By analyzing the time-dependent evolution of SARS-CoV-2 prevalence alongside the corresponding hospitalization and ICU occupancy rates, the model demonstrates that social distancing and lockdowns are essential for curbing the pandemic. The findings indicate that, without these interventions, ICU capacity would be exceeded within 10 to 15 days, resulting in approximately 1.5 million fatalities in the United States. Conversely, with these measures in place, the total death toll is projected to decrease by 80% to 90%.

Word embeddings have become a cornerstone of natural language processing, with context window size being a critical hyperparameter. While extensive research has focused on optimizing embedding representations, less attention has been paid to determining the ideal context window size. This study investigates how context window size affects downstream NLP tasks and proposes a straightforward, automated method for identifying the optimal size. We demonstrate that a larger window does not always yield better results; rather, the ideal setting varies by task. Furthermore, we introduce a new task-specific metric called the Context Window Score (CWS) to pinpoint superior window sizes. Our findings indicate that CWS effectively captures the impact of window size on task performance. We also present a novel approach for automatically detecting the optimal window size by leveraging the superior window information. Experiments across word similarity, sentence similarity, and sentiment analysis confirm that the proposed method is both effective and efficient.

This paper introduces a Lagrangian formulation for stars composed of spinning particles, extending the classic Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff (TOV) framework to the spinning regime. We establish the conservation laws of mass and energy, along with the momentum balance equation, by employing the stress-energy tensor. Furthermore, we examine the thermodynamic properties of spinning matter and derive the corresponding equations of state. Finally, we analyze the structural characteristics of spinning stars and derive the specific differential equations required to solve their internal profiles.

We investigate the Lemaître-Tolman-Bondi (LTB) spacetime within a Palatini $f(R)$ framework, where the Einstein-Hilbert action is modified by a function of the Ricci scalar, $f(R)$. Our analysis demonstrates that in this formalism, the modified Einstein equations yield an effective energy density that is non-zero, even when the scalar curvature vanishes. Consequently, the resulting equations of motion for the LTB metric resemble the standard General Relativity forms but include an effective energy density term. To determine the specific form of this density, we apply the weak-field limit of the modified gravity theory. Furthermore, we examine the singularity structure of the spacetime and find that the Birkhoff theorem holds in the modified theory, implying that the exterior vacuum solution is static and spherically symmetric.

Quantum nonlocality serves as a cornerstone of quantum information theory, yet it is highly fragile when subjected to noise. This fragility hinders the practical application of nonlocality in quantum communication and computing. In this work, we introduce a novel class of nonlocal correlations that exhibit robustness against noise, thereby surpassing the performance of standard quantum strategies. We demonstrate that certain instances within this new class defy any non-trivial bound established by Bell-type inequalities, a property unattainable by conventional correlations. Furthermore, we show that correlations from this family can be generated using multipartite quantum states. Specifically, we present a method to certify the non-classicality of these states by violating a set of inequalities derived from our new correlations, which remain robust even in the presence of noise.

This study introduces a novel approach for forecasting user visual attention on brief Windows, grounded in the analysis of gaze patterns. The core methodology involves extracting gaze features and applying a forecasting model to predict future visual focus. The authors evaluated the effectiveness of various feature sets and forecasting algorithms using a dataset derived from gaze recordings. The results demonstrate that these techniques achieve high accuracy in predicting user attention, and the study concludes by offering insights into the practical application of this forecasting model for broader use cases.

The reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) has emerged as a promising technology for enhancing wireless communication by enabling the programmable reflection of radio waves. This paper introduces a novel architecture for transmission-based RIS, designed to transmit radio waves from an integrated low-noise amplifier (LNA) alongside the reflective elements. This approach offers significant advantages over traditional reflection-based systems, including the ability to amplify weak signals and eliminate the need for individual phase shifters at each element. We present a comprehensive analysis of the proposed transmissive RIS design, covering its architecture, theoretical performance, and a practical prototype. Experimental results validate the design's functionality and confirm its potential for future 6G telecommunication applications.

Offline reinforcement learning (RL) involves learning a policy within a fixed dataset, a scenario where the agent cannot interact with the environment. While recent research has primarily focused on offline RL through linear function approximation, this paper investigates the broader context of offline RL using the universal function class. We propose a novel algorithm called Linear-Optimization (LO), which leverages the inherent offline RL structure to achieve the optimal minimax regret of $O(\sqrt{dH})$ for linear function approximation. This result is significant because LO attains the optimal regret bound for a wider class of universal function approximators, rather than being restricted solely to linear settings.

This paper examines collinear configurations within planar three-body problems, specifically analyzing scenarios where one body is significantly more massive than the others. We demonstrate that, in such mass hierarchies, collinear solutions are confined to two specific scenarios: either the lighter bodies align on opposite sides of the central massive object, or they position themselves on opposite sides with the central mass intermediate.

Fluorescence duration imaging microscopy (FLIM) is a powerful, label-free technique capable of distinguishing various cell types and detecting early signs of disease. However, the optical limitations of the microscope reduce the effective resolution of FLIM images, thereby blurring the boundaries between adjacent cells. To address this, we introduce a novel deconvolution framework designed to enhance FLIM image resolution. This approach employs a specific fluorescence point spread function (PSF) model to represent the microscope's blurring effect. By integrating a total variation regularization term, the method preserves the integrity of the resulting images. Furthermore, the proposed framework is formulated as a non-smooth optimization problem and resolved using the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM). Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed deconvolution method significantly improves image quality, offering greater clarity and detail compared to traditional approaches.

Product search systems are essential for e-commerce, yet traditional methods often fail to account for the diverse actions of users. This paper introduces a novel approach to modeling user behavior within search by leveraging graph neural networks. Specifically, we develop a deep graph convolutional network designed to capture the sequential patterns of user behavior. This architecture integrates a graph convolutional network for product representation alongside a recurrent neural network for modeling click sequences. This hybrid design enables the system to account for both the semantic content of products and their behavioral ordering. We evaluate our method on a large-scale product search dataset and demonstrate that it outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques.

This study introduces a new unsupervised graph embedding framework that leverages a learned deep manifold prior to construct an associated graph. The approach employs a deep autoencoder to derive a manifold representation of the data, thereby establishing a nonlinear mapping between the data and latent spaces. Subsequently, a similarity graph is built based on the latent features. The final graph embedding is achieved by jointly optimizing the deep manifold structure and the affinity graph through a unified objective function. Experimental results across various datasets demonstrate that the proposed method surpasses existing state-of-the-art techniques.

Non-orthogonal patterned designs are essential for achieving massive connectivity in grant-free random access. This paper introduces a new two-stage design strategy that integrates a genetic algorithm with a semi-orthogonal pattern generation technique. The initial stage utilizes a genetic algorithm to create a diverse pool of non-orthogonal candidates, while the second stage employs the generated semi-orthogonal patterns to refine the best candidates from that pool. This approach is designed to mitigate the high computational cost associated with traditional joint optimization methods. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed technique outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of user throughput and spectral efficiency.

This study introduces a novel encoder designed for combinatorially compressed sensing (CSS), which is a specialized subset of standard compressed sensing. The primary contribution is a new class of encoders derived from the XOR operation of two sparse vectors, which can be adapted to function as an encoder for CSS applications. We demonstrate that the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) performance of this encoder-based system exceeds that of conventional CSS systems utilizing random encoders. Furthermore, we provide a mathematical proof confirming this enhanced SNR performance.

This paper introduces a novel framework designed to enhance the generalization and resilience of domain adaptation models. The approach involves two key components: a resilient learning mechanism that leverages adversarial domain adaptation to boost generalization, and a new method for stochastic modification of the training data to further improve resilience. The adversarial component trains a domain adaptation model by treating the encoder as the generator and a discriminator as the adversary, thereby ensuring that the learned representations are domain-invariant and generalize well to unseen domains. Concurrently, the proposed stochastic modification technique generates diverse training samples by applying random transformations to the original data, which helps prevent overfitting and strengthens the model's robustness. Extensive experiments conducted on the standard domain adaptation benchmark datasets, specifically the OfficeHome and VisA2A sets, demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves state-of-the-art performance in both generalization capability and resilience to distribution shifts.

This paper establishes that all 2-local derivatives acting on the standard matrix Jordan algebras $M_{n}(K)$—where $K$ denotes either a commutative involutive ring or an infinite field—are proven to coincide with their underlying linear equivalent local derivatives. As a consequence of this result, the study extends to an explicit characterization of inner derivatives on $M_{n}(M)$, where $M$ represents any infinite $\sigma$-algebra.

The study investigates the gravitational lensing of a Dirac monopole within the context of Berry's phase. It demonstrates that the topological charge associated with this phase can undergo an alteration akin to the transition observed in the standard lensing of light. Furthermore, the research calculates the "shift effect" specifically for Berry's phase.

This study examines the spin-orbit coupling (SOC) impact on Bose-Einstein condensates, specifically analyzing the stability of compact solitons. By employing a Bogoliubov approximation, we investigate how spin-orbit coupling density affects system stability. Our findings indicate that SOC density influences stability, with a critical threshold below which the system becomes unstable. Furthermore, we analyze the spin-orbit density reliance regarding the stability of compact solitons.

The $\Lambda_c(2595)^+$, identified as the ground-state $\Lambda_c$ with $J^P=1/2^-$, is hypothesized to be the massive quark spin symmetry (MQSS) partner of the $\Lambda_c(2625)^+$, a $J^P=3/2^-$ excited state. This study examines MQSS in the context of the $\Lambda_c(2595)^+$ by analyzing its decay into $D^0\pi^-$ and $D^+$ $\pi^-$ channels. The analysis reveals that the $D^0\pi^-$ decay is suppressed relative to $D^+ \pi^-$, a pattern consistent with MQSS expectations. Furthermore, the $D^+$ $\pi^-$ decay is observed to be suppressed compared to the $D^*+\pi^+$ channel, a behavior that aligns with MQSS predictions. These findings support the conclusion that the $\Lambda_c(2595)^+$ and $\Lambda_c(2625)^+$ are indeed quark spin partners.

This note explores the estimation of a function $f$ defined on the set of orbits of a Lie group $G$ acting on a manifold $M$, where $f$ is a smooth extension from a class of functions on $M$. We demonstrate that for a dense subset of pairs $(M, f)$, the value of $f$ at any given point in $G\backslash M$ can be recovered, up to an arbitrarily small error, using data collected along the orbit of that point.

This white paper outlines the case for investigating axion-like particles (ALPs) at energy scales significantly beyond those reachable by the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). We examine the potential of future high-energy muon colliders to discover these ALPs, which are compelling candidates for physics beyond the Standard Model. These particles are characterized by their extremely weak coupling to photons and fermions, a feature that allows them to be produced at high rates in muon collisions despite these small couplings. We provide a detailed analysis of the production mechanisms and decay signatures for both light and heavy ALPs, demonstrating that upcoming muon colliders can probe a vast region of the ALP parameter space that is inaccessible to current experiments.

Metadata is essential for the effective management of data assets, yet the lack of a unified, open-source, and scalable metadata administration framework has hindered the adoption of cross-layer enhancements. To address this, we introduce MetaSys, a functional open-source framework designed to facilitate and evaluate these improvements. MetaSys offers a comprehensive set of tools for executing, assessing, and analyzing cross-layer enhancements, with its efficacy demonstrated through a case study on a data warehouse.

This study introduces transfer learning strategies for image classification that leverage both synthetic data and Siamese networks. Our approach involves pre-training a standard convolutional neural network (CNN) on a source dataset and fine-tuning it on a target dataset. We evaluate this method across three configurations: training the CNN on both datasets from scratch, fine-tuning a source-pretrained model on the target data, and fine-tuning a model pretrained on the target data on the same target data. Additionally, we propose a novel transfer learning technique using Siamese networks, where pre-training occurs on one dataset and subsequent fine-tuning occurs on the other. Our findings indicate that our proposed methods yield superior results compared to traditional transfer learning approaches.

This paper examines the existence of solutions for a class of quasilinear elliptic equations with a perturbation, given by
$$
-\Delta u = u^q + a(x)u^p + f(x) \quad \text{in } \mathbb{R}^N, \quad u > 0, \quad \lim_{|x|\to\infty} u(x) = 0,
$$
where $p, q > 0$, $f$ is a nonnegative function, and $a(x)$ is a nonnegative, locally integrable term. We establish that a nontrivial radially symmetric solution exists provided $p < \frac{N}{2}$, $q > \frac{N}{p}-N$, and $q > \frac{N}{2} - 1$. Furthermore, we demonstrate that no such solution exists if $p \geq \frac{N}{2}$.

Recurrent neural networks (RNNs) are a foundational element in deep learning, yet they face significant challenges in modeling long-term dependencies due to the vanishing gradient problem. This study introduces Fourier Recurrent Units (FRUs), a novel architecture designed to overcome these limitations. FRUs leverage Fourier series to model the recurrence function, thereby enabling the training of deep RNNs with long-range dependencies. We demonstrate that FRUs can be seamlessly integrated into existing RNN variants, such as vanilla RNNs, GRUs, and LSTMs. Empirical evaluations across multiple benchmarks indicate that these units substantially enhance performance in capturing long-term dependencies.

This paper introduces a novel Markov decision framework designed to guide navigation toward an optimal strategy. In this framework, a navigator traverses a graph toward a target destination, facing random disturbances at each step. These disruptions may either alter the direction of movement or shift the node being visited. The objective is to determine a navigation strategy that minimizes the expected number of steps required to reach the destination. We analyze the problem under two specific disturbance models: one where disturbances are defined by a graph-based distribution, and another where they follow a Poisson process. For both models, we establish an optimal strategy and derive the corresponding expected step counts.

We introduce a novel method for generating a highly brilliant, linearly polarized attosecond electron bunch using a two-stage injection process. In the first stage, electrons are injected into an electromagnetic field generated by a plasma lens, creating an extremely short electron pulse. In the second stage, this pulse is injected into another plasma wakefield where its energy is boosted. The resulting electron pulse features a duration of approximately 400 attoseconds and a linear polarization aligned with the accelerating wakefield's electric field. Theoretical analysis indicates that this approach can yield a peak electron brightness of $10^{21}$ A/m$^2$/sr, surpassing current state-of-the-art standards.

This article examines the concept of existence from an astronomical standpoint, focusing specifically on the emergence of life. It proposes that living systems are distinguished by their capacity to self-organize, organize themselves, and maintain their identity. To explain how living systems achieve this, the author introduces a new concept: "intricacy." This term describes the degree of self-organization within a system, defined as the number of distinct ways its components can be arranged. The article further explores the relationship between intricacy and entropy, arguing that while entropy measures disorder, intricacy measures order. It also discusses the connection between intricacy and complexity, suggesting that they are complementary but distinct concepts. Finally, the author presents a hypothesis that living systems are capable of increasing their own intricacy, thereby creating new forms of life.

Climate change is a critical global issue that demands extensive research and development (R&D) investment to address its causes and impacts. This study examines how R& D policy can be shaped by analyzing the landscape of climate change research available through publicly accessible scientific literature. We propose a method to extract and analyze this data, utilizing open archives and AI tools. This approach allows for the creation of a comprehensive, up-to-date map of the field, enabling the identification of key research areas, their evolution, and the institutions and nations driving innovation. The paper outlines the advantages and limitations of this methodology, demonstrating its potential to support evidence-based policy making.

The Android Native Development Kit (NDK) enables C/C++ code execution on Android devices, making it a critical target for security researchers. Although numerous studies have examined the NDK's security, a systematic, comprehensive review remains absent. This paper introduces ASVAAN, a framework designed to systematically analyze the NDK's source code. By utilizing the NDK's native channel, ASVAAN automatically gathers data on function calls, function pointers, and library dependencies. The analysis of the framework's output reveals that the NDK heavily depends on the C standard library, exposing the platform to various security vulnerabilities. Additionally, the study identifies that the NDK exposes sensitive data, such as the device's MAC address, to applications. Finally, the authors propose specific mitigation strategies to address these security and privacy concerns.

Blockchain technology has gained significant traction within the cryptocurrency sector, with Ethereum emerging as a leading blockchain platform. This study examines the temporal dynamics of the Ethereum blockchain's ego networks, which consist of the central node (the initiator) and its immediate neighbors in a transaction graph. We analyze these networks across multiple specific attributes, including transaction frequency, transaction value, and shared labels. Furthermore, we investigate how network characteristics evolve over time, specifically focusing on the ego networks' size and clustering coefficient.

The LaAlO$_3$/SrTiAl$_3$ (LAO/STO) interface is widely recognized for generating a two-dimensional electron system (2DES) that exhibits superconductivity and a quantum Hall effect. However, the underlying mechanisms driving these phenomena remain poorly understood. This study employs a quantum model to investigate the 2DES at the LAO/STO junction, specifically examining the interplay between electron-electron interactions and the substrate's quantum fluctuations. Our results indicate that the 2DES is highly sensitive to these fluctuations, which can either suppress superconductivity or trigger a transition into a metallic state. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the interaction between the 2DES and these fluctuations can be manipulated via external optical fields. Consequently, we propose a viable strategy for controlling the 2DES dynamics at the LAO/STO junction through optical manipulation.

This paper examines the relationship between two modal logics for linear deduction: pomset logic and bivariant logic. We demonstrate that pomset logic can be derived from bivariant logic by eliminating certain structural rules, and we identify the specific constraints on the bivariant modal operator required to establish the internal logic of presheaf categories. These findings offer a fresh perspective on the long-standing debate between linear lambda-calculus variants based on bivariant and pomset logic.

The Ding-Iohara-Miki (DIM) algebra, a non-commutative, associative algebra, is defined by the relations of two generators, $G_0$ and $G_1$, which embody the structure of the generalized elliptic Knizhnik-Zamolodchikov (elliptic KZ) equation. This paper demonstrates the validity of the pentagon relation within the DIM algebra by employing a factorization approach to the generalized elliptic KZ equation.

We introduce a novel photometric redshift algorithm, which is the first of its kind to utilize a comprehensive spectral energy range from 0.36 to 4.5 microns. This approach employs a constrained photometric redshift technique, ensuring that the observed photometry is always included in the spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting process. The algorithm's performance was evaluated using a simulated dataset comprising 10,000 galaxies with redshifts spanning from 0.01 to 4.00. The results demonstrate that the method achieves a median photometric redshift error of 0.015, a 20th percentile error of 0.003, and a 90th percentile error of 0.035. Furthermore, the algorithm's efficacy was tested on two real galaxy samples from the CDF-S and ELAIS-S1 regions, which were derived from the COSMOS2015 and COSMOS2016 catalogs. The application of this method to these real datasets yielded median photometric redshift errors of 0.016 and 0.017, respectively, alongside 20th percentile errors of 0.004 and 0.005, and 90th percentile errors of 0.034 and 0.036. This paper introduces a system designed to aid decision-making for energy system operators by utilizing a probabilistic approach. The core of this approach is a forecasting model that predicts future energy demand using historical data. The model's parameters are estimated via Bayesian inference, and the resulting probability distribution of energy demand guides the selection of optimal energy strategies. The primary objective is to fulfill energy demand at the lowest possible cost. The paper presents the methodology, outlines the necessary algorithms, and provides numerical results from tests conducted on actual data.

The Hartree-Fock wavefunction, which represents a single Slater determinant, exhibits an exact mapping to a matrix product state (MPS) with occupation number $N$. This mapping reveals that the reduced Hartree-Fock two-body density matrix corresponds to a specific MPS derived from a configuration of size Three. This result indicates that the two-body density matrix possesses a low entanglement structure, which explains the high efficiency of configuration interaction algorithms based on a single determinant. Furthermore, this correspondence suggests a natural extension: an $M$-body reduced density matrix can be represented as an MPS with occupation number $M+1$ derived from a configuration of size $M+2$.

We introduce a minimal framework featuring a non-abelian dark sector with a dark gauge group of $SU(2)_D$ and a dark fermion $\chi$ in the fundamental representation. The model incorporates a scalar doublet $\Phi$ that breaks the $SU(2)_D$ symmetry and acquires a mass via the Higgs mechanism. The dark matter candidate is identified as the $\chi$ fundamental fermion, which is produced through the decay of the Higgs-like scalar $\Phi$. Theoretical predictions for the dark matter relic density are derived from the annihilation cross-section of $\chi\chi$ into Standard Model particles mediated by $\Phi$. We demonstrate that the model successfully accounts for the observed relic density while addressing the long-standing $1\sigma$ discrepancy in the $(g-2)_\mu$ anomaly.

This study introduces a deep learning surrogate model for the Digital Twin Earth (DTE) system, specifically designed to simulate coastal inundation. The model utilizes neural operators to forecast water levels across a global grid, leveraging high-resolution topographical data and meteorological inputs. The approach employs a physics-informed architecture that integrates hydrodynamic equations to ensure adherence to fundamental physical laws. The model's efficacy is assessed using a combination of a realistic, high-resolution coastal dataset and a synthetic dataset generated via a hydrodynamic simulator. The results indicate that the model achieves an accuracy of 90% in predicting flooding events, with a prediction speed 100 times faster than traditional hydrodynamic simulators. The authors conclude that this method offers a robust, high-performance solution for DTE applications in coastal management.

The BeyondPlanck collaboration, a consortium of scientists dedicated to advancing cosmological research through the analysis of Planck data, has evolved into a model for open, reproducible science. This paper outlines the collaboration's development, its current capabilities, and its future trajectory. We examine the infrastructure supporting BeyondPlanck, emphasizing its role in facilitating reproducibility and ensuring long-term data preservation. Additionally, we highlight the contributions of the broader cosmological community, which has been essential in creating and refining the software tools and data products used by BeyondPlanck. The discussion concludes with an outline of the upcoming direction for Cosmoglobe, the entity succeeding BeyondPlanck, and its plans for sustaining and disseminating data products for the next decade.

Turing patterns, characterized by spatially periodic structures, are frequently observed in developmental biology. While recent research has identified these patterns in biological systems, the mechanisms driving their emergence remain unclear. This study investigates Turing motifs within reaction-diffusion networks, specifically focusing on the interaction between diffusion and limited transport. We demonstrate that restricted transport significantly influences pattern formation, shifting the system from a Turing state to a Turing-wrapped state. Furthermore, we observe that restricted transport enhances the stability of Turing motifs, with the system's response to perturbations improving as the transmission rate decreases.

This study explores the Yang-Mills framework within the context of quasiclassical behavior, specifically investigating how classical solutions to the Yang-Mills equations can emerge from the theory. We examine the conditions under which the quantum potential vanishes for Bohmian trajectories, thereby allowing the trajectories to follow classical paths. Additionally, we analyze the implications of this mechanism for the radiation problem associated with accelerated charges.

Bargaining dialogues serve as a cornerstone of multi-agent systems, yet current models often fail to adequately address adversarial behavior. This study introduces a novel adversarial training framework for these conversations by employing data augmentation techniques. Our approach involves creating adversarial examples by introducing noise to the training data, which subsequently trains models capable of handling adversary inputs. Furthermore, we propose a new metric for evaluating these interactions, termed the "bargaining gap," to measure the disparity between the final agreed-upon price and the ideal target. Experimental results demonstrate that this proposed method significantly reduces the bargaining gap compared to existing baselines.

This study investigates brane-world scenarios within five-dimensional Einstein-Maxwell-Dilaton-Brane actions, where the string tension is a dynamical variable subject to fluctuations across the extra dimension. We derive the corresponding equations of motion and subsequently employ the method of light-cone compactification to determine specific solutions. These solutions encompass a static, spherically symmetric black brane and a static, spherically symmetric (anti-)de Sitter black hole.

This study investigates the nonlinear statistical characteristics of gravitational wave signals from black hole mergers, specifically targeting the estimation of crucial physical parameters. We employ the Fisher information matrix to evaluate the estimation precision of the chirp mass and symmetric mass ratio, while utilizing the Kullback-Leibler divergence to quantify the information content of the gravitational wave signals. Our analysis demonstrates that the nonlinear statistical framework offers a robust and effective approach for estimating these fundamental black hole parameters.

This study presents a comprehensive historical dataset on the U.S. commercial shipping industry spanning 1966 to 2014, derived from the Bureau of Labor Statistics' Cost of Transport Series. The dataset includes real-dollar values for freight expenses, transportation volume, new ship construction, used vessel acquisition, and scrap valuation. The study also examines the real-price levels of new and used vessels. The findings indicate that real freight costs and volumes have declined over time, whereas costs regarding new ships have risen; however, costs for used vessels and scrap values have remained relatively stable. Additionally, the research reveals that new ship construction has become more capital-intensive, while the industry's labor intensity has increased for used acquisitions. The paper further analyzes the real-price dynamics of new versus used cargo vessels, concluding that new ships command a premium over their used counterparts.

This study evaluates the efficacy of web anomaly detectors in identifying malicious behavior. We conducted a systematic literature review to identify and assess detectors published between 2005 and 2018. Our analysis examined the detectors' attributes, the datasets used for evaluation, and their respective performance outcomes. The results indicate that these detectors achieve high performance, yet they are susceptible to overfitting. Furthermore, the literature reveals a scarcity of research on the operational lifespan of these detectors.

This study presents a novel approach for segmenting gliomas in brain MRI images by employing convolutional neural networks (CNNs) combined with innovative post-processing techniques. The proposed methodology utilizes a CNN to predict the probability of each voxel belonging to a specific tissue class, followed by a post-processing step that applies a graph-based algorithm to generate the final segmentation. This algorithm functions by identifying the shortest path from the tumor core to the surrounding edema. The core advantage of this approach lies in its minimal computational demands, as it relies on straightforward operations that can be efficiently executed on standard CPUs. Furthermore, the method is designed to be adaptable for various types of gliomas, including those with indistinct boundaries.

Triplons represent the elementary excitations in quantum antiferromagnets, characterized by spin 1 and lacking electric charge. These excitations emerge from the triplet pairing of neighboring antialignments. This study examines the thermodynamic characteristics of triplons within quantum antiferromagnets. Our analysis indicates that triplons manifest as a new type of quasiparticle, distinct from magnons. We demonstrate that triplons can be generated in bulk quantum antiferromagnets through the excitation of two photons with parallel polarization. Additionally, we explore the potential for creating room-temperature triplons and discuss the implications of these findings for the development of quantum information technologies.

This study introduces statistical convergence defined by a directed set, expanding the concept of Dostani\'{c}'s F-convergence. We establish several relevant properties and illustrate the approach with a set of examples.

This study introduces a non-continuous Galerkin finite element approach for solving the 1D Rosenau equation, utilizing the Crank-Nicolson scheme for time discretization. The proposed numerical framework demonstrates stability and convergence of first order in both space and time. Furthermore, the effectiveness of the numerical results is supported by several computational examples.

This study examines the well-posedness of coupled partial differential equations (PDEs) governing the interaction between compressible and incompressible fluids. The analysis employs a semigroup approach to establish a framework for these coupled PDEs, subsequently proving the existence of a unique solution within this framework. The resulting coupled system consists of a Navier-Stokes equation for the compressible component and a Stokes equation for the incompressible component, with their interface connected by a linear coupling operator. The interaction domain is defined as a subdomain within the three-dimensional space. The weak formulation of this coupled system is derived in a Hilbert space setting, and a Lax-Milgram-type theorem is applied to demonstrate solution existence and uniqueness.

We present a theoretical framework for analyzing charged excitons (excitons polarons) within van der Waals van der Waals heterostructures, specifically focusing on the transition from liquid to crystal phases induced by strong magnetic fields. Our analysis reveals that at intense magnetic fluxes, these excitons organize into a hexagonal lattice, a phenomenon termed magnetic-field-driven Wigner crystallization. This study examines the specific conditions required for this phase transition and investigates the resulting properties of the magnetic crystal state.
