Neural Machine Translation (NMT) has achieved significant success in producing translations of high quality. However, despite this progress, current state-of-the-art models often fall short of the quality levels found in professional bitexts. This paper investigates whether leveraging existing high-quality NMT translations can enhance the quality of lower-tier bitexts. We introduce a novel dataset comprising 120,000 sentence pairs, where each translation is generated by applying controlled noise to the original reference text. This noise is specifically designed to degrade translation quality in a manner that mimics the errors found in lower-tier bitexts. We then evaluate the effectiveness of using NMT systems trained on this noisy data to recover the original high-quality references. Our findings indicate that NMT models trained on noisy data outperform those trained on lower-tier bitexts, demonstrating that NMT can successfully reverse the effects of controlled noise and restore high-quality translations.

The transition from logarithmic to area-law scaling of entanglement entropy in one-dimensional quantum many-body systems is a significant phenomenon that has been extensively investigated. In this work, we demonstrate that this shift can be engineered by incorporating engineered dissipation into a one-dimensional spin chain. Our analysis reveals that the system's long-time entanglement entropy evolves through three distinct phases: a short-time regime characterized by logarithmic scaling, an intermediate phase exhibiting a logarithmic power-law increase, and the long-time regime following an area law. Furthermore, we observe that the intermediate phase disappears when the system size is small. These results offer valuable insights into the dynamics of entanglement in open quantum many-body systems.

We examine the spin-orbit interaction within heterostructure flat bands, specifically in systems where a transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) monolayer is encapsulated by a TMD alloy. This interaction arises from the electric field generated by the alloy, which induces orbital polarization in the monolayer. We demonstrate that the resulting spin-orbit coupling is highly tunable through adjustments to the alloy's composition.

Quantum reservoir computing is a machine learning framework that leverages the intrinsic complex and often difficult-to-analyze dynamics of physical systems as a computational resource. This work investigates how environmental noise influences the performance of a quantum reservoir computer composed of a single qubit interacting with a thermal bath. We demonstrate that thermal noise can be advantageous, as it enables the quantum reservoir to achieve higher classification accuracy than its noise-free counterpart. Furthermore, we introduce a novel quantum reservoir architecture based on a single qubit coupled to two distinct thermal baths.

This study introduces a method for trapping atoms within an optical dipole trap formed by two counter-propagating 789 nm laser beams, the surface of which is a GaN-on-sapphire wafer. We demonstrate that the wafer's surface topography is sufficiently flat to ensure that atoms remain confined in the trap without significant interference from the surface.

This paper presents a comparison of mixed and Lagrange finite element approaches for solving Poisson's equation, utilizing the MFEM library to implement both methods. The study involves constructing a Lagrange element of order $k$ and a mixed formulation based on a Raviart-Thomas element of order $k-1$, with a specific focus on the implications of the inf-sup condition. Numerical results indicate that the discrete inf-sup constant for the mixed formulation is significantly influenced by mesh refinement, whereas the Lagrange constant remains stable.

This study investigates a class of sign-changing interacting dark energy models defined by $Q = 3\beta H\rho_d$ and an equation of state $w_d = \alpha H$, where both $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are constant parameters. Utilizing the Markov Chain Monte Carlo method, we constrain the parameters of these models based on observational data, including Type Ia supernovae, baryon acoustic oscillations, and cosmic microwave background radiation. Our analysis indicates that the model is viable for $\alpha = -1.0^{+0.2}_{-0.3}$ and $\beta = 0.0^{+0.2}_{-0.3}$. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the dark matter and dark energy densities converge to equality at the present epoch, suggesting a significant role for this interaction in cosmic evolution. Finally, we analyze the dynamical stability of these scenarios and examine their implications for statefinder diagnostics.

The radio burst known as a Fast Radio Burst (FRB) is hypothesized to originate from a tidal disruption event (TDE) involving a compact object and a black hole. This study examines the radio emission generated by a compact object interacting with a black hole across a range of parameters. We demonstrate that the compact object can be accelerated to high velocities by a quasi-perpendicular shock arising from the interaction between the black hole's accretion flow and the TDE ejecta. This shock acceleration can boost the object to speeds approaching the local sound speed, enabling it to penetrate the accretion disk and reach the central region. We propose that the radio bursts observed from FRBs result from the radio emission produced by the shock-heated plasma as the accelerated compact object penetrates the accretion disk. This mechanism is viable for a broad spectrum of parameters, including stellar-mass black holes interacting with neutron stars or white dwarfs, as well as supermassive black holes interacting with stellar-mass objects.

Acoustic cavitation, defined as the formation, growth, and collapse of microbubbles, is a phenomenon widely utilized in medical therapies and industrial processes. This study examines the dynamics of resonating microbubbles using a time-domain approach. We demonstrate that bubble dynamics can be effectively described by a modified Rayleigh-Pleset equation, which incorporates the effects of acoustic radiation pressure. Furthermore, we derive an analytical solution for the linearized version of this equation, which is applied to analyze the time-domain behavior of resonating microbubbles. Our findings indicate that the time-domain characteristics of these bubbles are governed by the acoustic radiation pressure force, a parameter that can be adjusted by varying the driving frequency.

This study introduces a novel framework for identifying tension in multimodal dialogues, leveraging emotion acknowledgment as a supplementary task. The core architecture consists of two sequential tasks: an acknowledgment module that detects the emotions of the preceding speaker, followed by a tension identification module that leverages the output from the former to predict tension levels. We introduce MUSER, a new dataset comprising 1,000 turns of Chinese multimodal dialogues annotated with both emotional states and tension levels. Experimental results demonstrate that MUSER significantly outperforms the existing Chinese tension dataset, CMUT-100, across various models. Furthermore, our evaluations confirm that the proposed MUSER framework achieves superior performance compared to single-task models dedicated solely to tension detection.

PanGEA is a toolkit designed to annotate expansive, semi-structured environments, such as those found in robotics research. It offers a web-based interface for constructing these environments and includes tools for exporting them in various formats. The system supports labeling nodes and edges with both categorical and continuous attributes, as well as defining relationships between them. Additionally, it facilitates the creation and implementation of custom functions to annotate edges and nodes.

The "downsizing" phenomenon describes the trend where star-forming galaxies appear at earlier cosmic epochs, a trend that contradicts the predictions of standard single-burst galaxy formation models. This study utilizes the IllustrisTNG simulation to examine downsizing, incorporating two critical refinements to the sub-grid physics: a metallicity-dependent initial mass function (IMF) and a supernova Ia (SNIa) rate that evolves with the stellar mass of galaxies. Our results indicate that these updates significantly alter the star-formation histories of simulated galaxies. Specifically, the metallicity-dependent IMF reduces the star-formation rate (SFR) of massive elliptical galaxies by approximately 20% in the present day, while the SNIa rate refinement reduces it by an additional 10%. Consequently, the combined effects of these updates reduce the SFR of massive elliptical galaxies by roughly 30% today. This reduction in the SFR of massive elliptical galaxies is primarily driven by a lower SFR in the simulation's earlier history, which in turn is caused by the updated sub-grid physics. Furthermore, the study demonstrates that the refined sub-grid physics leads to a more realistic star-formation history for massive elliptical galaxies, characterized by a more gradual decline in the SFR.

This study introduces a novel approach to image compressive sensing (CS) reconstruction that leverages the inherent sparsity of natural imagery. The core concept involves sparsely representing an entire image as a sparse linear combination of a minimal subset of representative image patches. The proposed framework integrates a non-linear regularization technique to enforce this collective sparse structure, thereby enhancing reconstruction quality. The paper first reviews the standard CS reconstruction model and subsequently introduces a non-linear regularization strategy that maintains the global collective sparse structure. The proposed method is validated through numerical experiments, which demonstrate its effectiveness in reconstructing images from CS measurements.

Identifying skin conditions from images is a critical task for dermatology, yet current deep learning models often struggle with accuracy due to the complex nature of skin issues. This study introduces RethNet, a novel framework designed to enhance the identification of these issues by leveraging the distinct characteristics of each item on a skin surface. The architecture consists of two key components: a region-specific module that processes individual areas of the image, and a global module that captures the overall context of the image. These modules are integrated through a new item-by-item learning mechanism, which utilizes a specialized loss function to optimize training. Experimental results demonstrate that RethNet outperforms existing state-of-the-art models in identifying various skin conditions. Furthermore, the proposed method exhibits robust generalization capabilities when applied to the Skin-IT dataset.

This work examines the efficiency and complexity of sequential decoding for PAC codes, specifically analyzing the PAC Gilbert-Hartley algorithm. We demonstrate that the expected runtime of the decoder is sub-exponential in code length, provided the channel error probability is sufficiently low. Furthermore, we establish that the algorithm's runtime exhibits sub-exponential behavior in expectation whenever the information rate is kept below a specific threshold. These findings are derived through a rigorous analysis of the branching factor within the decoding tree.

Cold-start users, who possess minimal interaction history, present a significant challenge for recommender systems. While existing methods often rely on collaborative filtering, they struggle to effectively utilize sparse data from these new users. To address this, we introduce a novel sequential suggestion framework designed to leverage information from both new users and established ones. Our approach utilizes meta-learning to rapidly adapt mature models to new contexts, employing a meta

The origins of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs) remain a significant unsolved mystery in astrophysics. While the leading hypothesis attributes these particles to extragalactic sources, recent findings suggest that galactic origins are also plausible. This overview examines the current state of research on UHECRs, highlighting key observational evidence supporting a galactic provenance.

The DART mission marks the inaugural active planetary defense test, aiming to alter the orbit of the Didymos binary asteroid system by colliding a kinetic impactor with the smaller moon, Dimorphos. This study examines how the projectile's shape influences the momentum transfer to Dimorphos, analyzing the effects of various geometries—including spheres, ellipsoids, and cylinders—on the impactor's mass, velocity, and the resulting change in Dimorphos's momentum. The research demonstrates that momentum transfer is contingent upon the projectile's shape, with the coefficient of momentum ($Q$) varying significantly across different geometries. Specifically, $Q$ is shown to depend on the projectile's density, initial impact velocity, and the ratio of its characteristic dimensions. The findings indicate that for a fixed mass and velocity, the maximum momentum transfer occurs with a sphere, whereas elongated shapes such as ellipsoids and cylinders yield lower values. Additionally, the study assesses the impact of DART's actual impactor shape on the mission's outcomes, concluding that the observed reduction in Dimorphos's orbital period aligns with theoretical predictions.

This study introduces the MU-Net, a high dynamic interval fusion network designed for operator recognition from in-vehicle video. The architecture integrates a specialized high dynamic range (HDR) module that synthesizes a single HDR image from multiple frames captured at varying exposure levels. This approach enhances the clarity of both bright and dark regions within the image. The resulting HDR data is then processed by a unified recurrent neural network (RNN) that leverages temporal information to identify drivers. The MU-Net framework is built upon a hierarchical structure of interval networks (INs), where each IN functions as a distinct RNN. The system's capacity to adapt to diverse lighting conditions stems from the high dynamic module, while its ability to capture temporal dependencies arises from the sequential processing inherent in the recurrent neural networks. The MU-Net was evaluated using a dataset comprising 1,000 images featuring 12 drivers across 12 different lighting conditions. The results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques in operator recognition.

The Open Source Programming Language Community (OSPLC) is a decentralized ecosystem where individuals collaborate to create, share, and refine programming languages. Although OSPLC has seen significant growth, it faces persistent challenges, including the scarcity of trustworthy information, the prevalence of misinformation, and the resulting negative impacts on community health. To address these issues, we introduce the Extensive Blurb Archive Network (EBAN), a proposed network architecture designed to enhance information sharing and retrieval within OSPLCs. This paper outlines the EBAN's design principles, implementation strategies, and key advantages. Furthermore, we identify critical research gaps and outline potential directions for future development.

This study examines multistage estimators designed for estimating the average treatment effect (ATE) within a framework where subjects may abandon the study at any point, resulting in missing covariates or incomplete outcome data. Unlike conventional estimators that rely on complete data for all units, these multistage approaches utilize observations available at each specific stage. We introduce a generalized estimator that encompasses various existing methods, including inverse probability weighting, regression-based models, and the missing-indicator technique. This estimator is derived through the application of missingness indicators and can be implemented using standard statistical software. We demonstrate its asymptotic normality and provide a closed-form formula for its variance. Furthermore, we establish that the estimator is consistent and asymptotically efficient, provided that appropriate assumptions are met. We also outline the bias introduced by applying these estimators when assumptions are violated. Finally, we present a simulation study to evaluate the estimator's finite-sample performance.

This paper examines the convergence of iterative algorithms for the complete elliptic integral of the first kind, defined as $K(k) = \frac{\pi}{2} \int_0^{\pi/2} \frac{d\theta}{\sqrt{1-k^2\sin^2\theta}}$. These methods, which utilize the inverse hyperbolic tangent, are characterized by their simplicity and rapid convergence, making them highly effective for numerical computation. The convergence of such methods has been established in prior research, notably by S. M. Ostroverkhov in 2009, who demonstrated that the iteration $k_{n+1} = \tanh\left(\frac{\pi}{2} \frac{K^2(k_n)}{\pi^2 + 4K^2(k_n)\ln^2(4/K(k_n))}\right)$ yields a limit of $k=0$ for any initial $k_n \in (0,1)$. Building on this, the current study investigates the rate of convergence for the iteration $k_{n+1} = \tanh\left(\frac{\pi}{2} \frac{K^2(k_n)}{\pi^2 + 4K^2(k_n)\ln^2(4/K(k_n))}\right)$, specifically analyzing the behavior of the sequence $k_n$ as it approaches zero.

This study introduces a novel approach to Inductive Method Learning (IML), a technique that has recently gained traction for solving inverse problems. IML involves learning a mapping from a data-driven perspective, where the method is applied to a set of training examples to generalize over the space of interest. While prior research has largely focused on learning IMLs for linear inverse problems, this work extends the framework to handle nonlinear scenarios. We achieve this by decomposing the method into a sequence of linear operators, where each component is learned individually. This strategy offers two key advantages: it enables the use of extensive, high-quality datasets to train each sub-operator, and it facilitates the creation of efficient, interpretable methods by leveraging established linear IMLs. We validate our approach through experiments on both linear and nonlinear problems, demonstrating that it outperforms existing state-of-the-art IMLs.

The proliferation of fake news on social media has become a critical issue, with its detrimental effects on individuals and society prompting urgent attention. This study introduces a novel deep learning framework designed to detect and generate altered fake news in Arabic. The model employs a hybrid architecture combining Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) networks. Initially, the model processes news content and comments through a CNN layer to extract features, which are subsequently analyzed by the LSTM component to classify the authenticity of the news. Additionally, the LSTM module identifies the specific sections of the text responsible for the fake news classification. Experimental results indicate that this CNN-BiLSTM architecture outperforms other models, achieving a 99.1% accuracy rate in fake news detection and a 97.1% accuracy rate in fake comment detection.

In this correction notice, we amend a previous publication where we examined the torsion subgroup for an elliptic curve defined over the compositum of all $D_4$ extensions over the rational numbers. The update addresses a specific oversight in our earlier classification of the torsion group for $E(\mathbb{Q}(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{d_1}, \sqrt{d_2})))$, where $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{d_1}, \sqrt{d_2})$ represents a $D_4$ extension over $\mathbb{Q}$.

This study examines the dynamics of multiqubit systems subject to both coherent and incoherent noise, with a specific focus on the evolution of nonlocal correlations. We demonstrate that coherent noise can generate nonlocality even in the absence of incoherent noise, while incoherent noise alone can induce nonlocality within initially local states. Furthermore, we find that both noise types can cause nonlocal states to transition into local ones. Our analysis reveals that incoherent noise can induce nonlocality in states that would otherwise remain local under purely coherent noise. Finally, we investigate the relationship between these noise types and the emergence of nonlocal properties in the GHZ state.

Web scraping is a critical technique for extracting information from websites, yet it often encounters obstacles such as inconsistent page layouts, dynamic content, and anti-scraping defenses. While existing methods typically rely on manually crafted regular expressions or fragile XPath queries, this approach introduces significant maintenance burdens and fragility. To address these challenges, this paper introduces a reinforcement learning (RL) framework designed to automate the creation of targeted scraping logic. By modeling a scraping task as a tree-structured Markov Decision Process (MDP), our method enables the automatic derivation of an RL policy that generates XPath queries tailored to specific data targets. We validate this approach across various real-world web scraping scenarios, demonstrating that our automated method achieves performance comparable to, and in some cases superior to, manually crafted solutions.

This paper presents a framework for organizing Event Information in event-centric NLP tasks, specifically focusing on information about objects involved in an event. We propose a taxonomy that breaks down object-focused information into distinct categories, covering both the event participants themselves and supplementary attributes. Additionally, we introduce a corresponding representation system designed to capture this nuanced information. Through the use of instance and variation examples, we demonstrate how this representation effectively handles event components and their specific variations.

This study introduces a novel method for wavefield reconstruction that leverages limited-subspace weighted matrix decompositions. The approach is designed to recover a complete wavefield from a limited set of seismic measurements, utilizing a limited number of subspace weights to capture the full spatial extent of the data. The proposed technique is evaluated against a suite of synthetic datasets, demonstrating that it achieves superior results compared to existing methods.

Metalenses have garnered significant attention for their capacity to deliver high-resolution imaging across a wide spectrum. However, the performance of these lenses is often constrained by the complex dispersion of metasurfaces, which restricts their operational bandwidth. This study introduces a broadband quadratic metalens capable of capturing a broad field of view. The lens utilizes a design based on anisotropic Huygens' sources, which allow for the independent control of both the phase and the polarization state of transmitted light. This specific design strategy effectively mitigates dispersion, thereby enhancing the lens's bandwidth. Theoretical analysis and numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed lens maintains a Strehl ratio exceeding 0.8 from 400 to 1200 nm. Furthermore, the lens exhibits a wide field of view of 80° at 800 nm, with a relative aperture of f/1.6.

This study presents a 2D simulation and modeling framework for a non-neutral plasma system consisting of radio-frequency atmospheric-pressure plasma jets. The system comprises two parallel, collimated plasma streams separated by a plasma-free zone, which is subsequently overlaid by a grid of parallel electrodes. The model incorporates the Poisson equation, the Poisson-Nernst-Einstein equations, and the continuity equations to describe the plasma dynamics. The resulting simulations reveal that the plasma streams exhibit non-neutral characteristics, with one primarily populated by electrons and the other by ions. Furthermore, the study demonstrates that the interaction between these streams is driven by space-charge forces, causing them to repel one another. The influence of the external electrode grid on the streams is also examined, showing that the streams can be steered and confined by applying appropriate voltages to the grid. The findings suggest that this non-neutral plasma configuration could serve as a viable method for generating a non-neutral plasma beam.

This study investigates the quasinormal frequencies of $d$-dimensional black holes using the string-corrected metric proposed by Chong et al. (2019), specifically within the eikonal limit. By applying the WKB approximation, we determine the frequencies for scalar, vector, and tensor perturbations. Our analysis reveals that the frequencies are sensitive to the spacetime dimension, the perturbation type, and the string-corrected parameter. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the imaginary components of these frequencies diminish as the string-corrected parameter increases. Finally, we derive the analytical forms of the frequencies for the scalar, vector, and tensor modes in the extreme limit of black holes.

Pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) are currently the premier method for detecting nanohertz gravitational waves (GWs). This technique involves measuring the arrival times of radio pulses from pulsars, which are then analyzed for timing residuals that could indicate GW signals. While past research has primarily focused on cross-correlation techniques to identify GWs, this study introduces an alternative strategy that examines common-band noise directly. This approach offers a distinct advantage: it allows for the simultaneous analysis of both GW signals and common noise sources, such as those from the galactic center, thereby enhancing GW detection sensitivity. To demonstrate the method's efficacy, we applied it to data from the Parkes Pulsar Timing Array (PPTA) using 10 pulsars. Our results indicate that the common-band noise analysis successfully detected the Hellings-Downs (HD) correlation signature, which is a hallmark of GWs. Furthermore, the estimated amplitude of the GW signal aligns with the upper limits established by the cross-correlation method.

This study establishes necessary and sufficient conditions for the validity of support constraints on generator matrices within families of generalized Hamming weights (GHW) of an optimal linear Minimum Rank (MRD) code. The proof relies on a newly devised, algorithmic approach to calculating the rank of specific submatrices formed by the generator matrix.

This study investigates matrix-valued truncated Toeplitz operators on model spaces $ \mathcal{K}^2 (u) $, where $ u $ serves as an inner function and the symbol $ a $ is a bounded or bounded below bounded operator-valued function mapping $ L^2 (e^u \mathbb{C}) $ to itself. We establish conditions under which these operators remain bounded and determine their specific forms for cases involving $ u(z) = e^{\alpha \log(1 - \xi)} $ with $ \alpha > 0 $. Additionally, we examine the kernel structure of such operators, $ \mathcal{K}^2 (u) $, and introduce the concept of "equivalence post extension" to analyze the relationships between equivalence classes of truncated Toeplitz operators.

This study examines Bayesian marketing strategies for a product across multiple campaigns. In every instance, the firm must decide whether to promote the product or not, with the primary goal of maximizing the total number of sales. The central challenge is to determine which trials warrant a promotion. We introduce a fresh approach called the Bayesian Influence Successive Trials (Bayes-IST) method, which leverages a Markovian model of consumer purchasing behavior. This model incorporates two key drivers: individual consumer characteristics and the impact of prior advertising. By utilizing a greedy algorithm, Bayes-IST identifies the optimal sequence of trials for promotion. We also develop a theoretical framework to analyze Bayes-IST, demonstrating that it achieves a competitive ratio of at least 1/2, which converges to 1 under specific conditions. Furthermore, we benchmark Bayes-IST against a standard greedy heuristic and an exhaustive search method through simulations, revealing that it outperforms all alternatives.

This study presents a novel framework for unsupervised anomaly detection in audio, designed to operate without labeled data. The approach integrates the unsupervised dimensionality reduction technique UMAP with a clustering algorithm to identify anomalies. We evaluate this framework against two distinct datasets: one featuring labeled anomalies and another containing only normal audio. Under supervised conditions, the system successfully detects anomalies, whereas in unsupervised settings, it identifies audio samples that are most likely to contain anomalies. We further assess the system's robustness regarding domain shifts by training it on one dataset and testing it on a different one.

We examine the magnetic characteristics of a dilute SU(N) Fermi gas, where the system is composed of a majority of spin-up fermions and a minority of spin-down fermions. The system exhibits a magnetic phase diagram that includes a large paramagnetic region, a small ferromagnetic region, and an intermediate ferromagnetic phase characterized by a mixture of both. This intermediate state arises from the formation of a "magnetic soliton," a ferromagnetic domain that moves through a ferromagnetic background. The system's energy is determined by the number of these solitons, which can be calculated using a random phase approximation. The study also investigates the system's magnetic susceptibility and magnetization, revealing a phase transition from a paramagnetic to a ferromagnetic state as the minority fermion concentration increases.

This study examines the stacking of Fermi-LAT gamma-ray pulsar data to determine whether multi-wavelength observations can enhance the detection of gamma-ray signals. We analyzed pulsars with periods under 100 ms, which possess well-established spin-down rates, and compared their spin-down luminosities against stacked gamma-ray fluxes across various energy bands. Our findings indicate that the stacked gamma-ray fluxes align with spin-down luminosities at the 90% confidence level for energies above 100 MeV, a sensitivity that improves to 95% for periods shorter than 100 ms. Additionally, we explored the correlation between gamma-ray fluxes and optical luminosity, observing a strong positive relationship for fluxes exceeding 100 MeV. However, we note that the current sample's gamma-ray fluxes are limited by the low detection threshold of the Fermi-LAT instrument.

This study examines the spectral properties of fractional quantum Hall systems under a finite magnetic field. We demonstrate that the spectral density exhibits a series of well-defined magnetorotons, with their count increasing as the chemical potential rises. Conversely, when the chemical potential is sufficiently low, the spectral density can be precisely represented by the spectral components of single-excitation states. We also analyze the connection between this structured spectral density and the Laughlin wave function, as well as its relationship to the edge state framework.

The Intense Energy Occurrences experiment (IEO), a ground-based observatory situated in the Chilean Atacama Desert, aims to measure the energy spectra of ultra-high energy cosmic rays (UHECRs) with energies exceeding $10^{18.5}$ eV. The facility employs a dual approach: a ground array of 1,280 water Cherenkov tanks to detect air shower particles and an extensive air shower array of 16 Cherenkov telescopes to capture fluorescence light from the same events. This paper outlines the scientific objectives of the project, details the experimental setup, and presents a comprehensive analysis of the telescope system's performance.

This paper investigates the well-posedness of the Cauchy problem for the truncated Boltzmann equation, where the truncation is applied to large collision energies. The analysis establishes global existence and uniqueness for small initial data in $L^1 \cap L^\infty \cap B_{\infty, 1}^0$ across the entire phase space. Additionally, the study demonstrates that the global solution converges to the truncated Maxwellian as t approaches infinity, provided the initial distribution is close to it.

The rise of large-scale datasets has driven the development of powerful machine learning models, yet these models often struggle with noisy data, particularly labels that are incorrect. This study investigates how various machine learning algorithms perform under label noise, specifically analyzing the impact of noise levels on accuracy. We demonstrate that while deep learning models remain highly accurate even with substantial noise, traditional machine learning algorithms are significantly more susceptible to data corruption.

This study examines the automorphism groups associated with orbits of cyclic codes over finite fields. We introduce a novel class of symmetries termed "orbit codes," which are subsets of code vectors formed by applying an automorphism group to any single generating vector. We demonstrate that every such orbit consists of exactly one orbit code and establish necessary and sufficient conditions for two distinct orbit codes to share an automorphism group. Additionally, we explore the link between cyclic codes and their corresponding orbit codes, proving that every cyclic code is equivalent to one that shares the same orbit code under equivalence. We further derive that any orbit code possesses an automorphism group isomorphic to a specific subgroup of the group defining the underlying orbit. Finally, we provide illustrative examples of orbit codes along with their respective automorphism groups.

We report the discovery of a binary system within the open cluster M67, identified through the Kepler mission's Q1-Q16 data. This system, designated K2-138, exhibits a period of 10.3 days and a radial velocity semi-amplitude of 1.03 m/s. The system consists of a 0.93 M$_\odot$ turnoff star and a 0.16 M$_\odot$ brown dwarf companion. By combining these measurements with the cluster's age, we derive a precise mass for the turnoff star of 0.803 $\pm$ 0.006 M$_\odot$. This value aligns closely with the mass of the cluster's most massive stars, thereby confirming M67's age of 12.24 $\pm$ 0.8 Gyr.

This paper addresses the sufficiency problem concerning the framework of eigenfunctions associated with the complex Schrödinger operator $\mathscr{L}_c=-d^2/dx^2+cx^\alpha$. We establish that the framework of eigenfunctions for $\mathscr{L}_c$ is complete provided $c$ is complex ($c\in\mathbb{C}$) and the parameter $\alpha$ satisfies $\alpha\in(0,1)$.

This study introduces a conservative, density-driven smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) method enhanced with a specific formulation of the partition of unity. The approach utilizes a newly developed, high-order, and conservative estimator for calculating density and its derivatives, which is designed to be more accurate than traditional gradient approximation techniques. The method's stability and performance were evaluated through a series of standard benchmark tests, including the Zeldovich, Sedov, and Rayleigh-Taylor instabilities. The results demonstrate that this improved formulation of the density gradient significantly enhances overall method accuracy. Furthermore, the paper examines the impact of the density gradient formulation on the SPH equation of state and the equation of state itself. The findings indicate that the improved density gradient formulation can be applied to any equation of state without loss of effectiveness.

This study introduces a pixel-sensitive deep function-blend network designed to enhance the spectral resolution of hyperspectral images. The proposed method integrates two key components: a spectral fusion module that generates synthetic high-resolution spectral bands by combining multiple low-resolution inputs, and a pixel-sensitive deep network that applies a pixel-wise enhancement strategy to restore the original spectral reflectance curves. The resulting spectral information is subsequently restored using a deep learning-based reconstruction module. Experimental results demonstrate that the suggested approach outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in both spectral resolution and image quality.

This paper introduces Context Sensitive Object Geotagging (CSOG), a novel approach designed to extract meaningful semantic information from image objects by leveraging their surrounding context. CSOG operates through a two-stage pipeline: first, an object detection module identifies and localizes relevant items within an image, and second, a context-sensitive module classifies these objects based on the scene's background. This second stage utilizes a two-step process that begins by analyzing the object's foreground against the image's background to generate a context vector, which is then combined with the object's visual features to produce a context-aware feature representation. This enhanced representation is subsequently processed by a classifier to determine the object's specific semantic category. We evaluated CSOG using the COCO dataset for object detection and the MSCOCO-derived context dataset for classification. The results demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques in both object detection and context-sensitive classification.

The integration of remote sensing technology into hydrological modeling has significantly advanced the capability to assess dam storage levels. However, the widespread adoption of this technology is hindered by the high costs of acquiring and processing satellite imagery, as well as the complexity involved in interpreting these data. To address these barriers, this study introduces a novel, automated method for estimating dam storage change that relies on freely accessible, open-source software. The approach utilizes the Sentinel-2 satellite constellation and employs a metric derived from the difference between the difference of normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) images. This method was validated using data from 12 dams in the Upper Danube basin, where the results were benchmarked against official reservoir operation records. The study further demonstrates that the accuracy of the storage change estimates can be enhanced by applying a specialized calibration process. This calibration utilizes a training set of 100 images from the same region, which are labeled based on the initial method's outputs. The study concludes that the proposed approach is highly effective for monitoring dam storage change and offers a practical solution for hydrological applications.

The QFS-zone represents a specific region within the event horizon of a Schwarzschild black hole, situated between the event horizon and the photon sphere. This study examines the properties of this zone, specifically its volume and surface area, and further analyzes the characteristics of orbits located within it.

This study examines the impact of earnings calls on stock price movements by utilizing a novel dataset comprising transcripts from calls between 2004 and 2019. We developed a framework to automatically extract key information from transcripts, including earnings per share (EPS) guidance, forward-looking statements, and management guidance. Our analysis reveals that the magnitude of the stock price fluctuation immediately following an earnings call is directly proportional to the gap between the reported EPS and the analyst consensus estimate. Additionally, we identified that the stock price volatility in the three days post-call is significantly correlated with the tone of the management's remarks during that call.

This study addresses the challenge of placing sensors within a two-dimensional area to monitor a target, where each sensor has a fixed detection range and must communicate with a base station via a restricted radio link. The primary goal is to identify the minimum number of sensors required to guarantee target detection. The authors introduce a heuristic algorithm designed to solve this optimization problem. Additionally, they examine the impact of sensor heterogeneity on placement strategies. The analysis covers both scenarios: sensors with uniform target detection capabilities and those with diverse detection profiles.

This study introduces a novel quantum eigenstate selection (QES) algorithm designed to extract a specific eigenstate from a quantum state encoding the complete spectrum of a Hamiltonian. By integrating quantum amplitude estimation with generalized Kolmogorov-Gabor polynomial filters, the proposed QES method achieves an exponential speedup in runtime compared to existing QES approaches. The algorithm's efficacy is demonstrated through its application to linear system resolution via quantum phase estimation. Furthermore, we establish a new lower bound for the runtime of quantum phase estimation, proving that the current best-runtime implementation is optimal up to a polylogarithmic factor.

The study introduces a novel class of self-dual compact gauged infant skyrmions within a non-linear materials framework. In this model, the skyrmions' size is determined by the specific gauging function, which is further modulated by the spatially varying non-linear field. The system's energy is minimized by adjusting the magnitude of the non-linear field, and the resulting energy barrier is reduced by increasing the skyrmions' number density. These findings suggest that gauged infant skyrmions could be engineered in non-linear materials with tunable stability and size.

This study examines the phenomenology of the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) at the LHC, concentrating on the interplay between Higgs boson production and decay, as well as Drell-Yan processes. We analyze the impact of dimension-six operators, specifically those governing Higgs production and decay, on the Higgs transverse momentum spectrum and the invariant dilepton mass distribution from Higgs decays. Furthermore, we explore the consequences of higher-order operators, such as those affecting the Z boson's couplings, on the transverse momentum profile of the Z boson. Our findings demonstrate that these SMEFT operators can induce substantial deviations in the high-pT tails of the distributions, potentially reaching magnitudes of 100% or more. Consequently, we propose a novel approach for extracting SMEFT operator coefficients by performing differential analyses of Higgs and Z boson production.

A rotation gyroscope is a mechanical device that relies on the angular momentum generated by a spinning object to resist changes in its orientation. The diamond nuclear rotation gyroscope (DNCG) represents a proposed quantum mechanical analog to this device. In this system, the angular momentum is supplied by the collective spin of the nucleus, which is maintained in a stable orientation through the application of external magnetic fields. We have successfully demonstrated a functional prototype of the DNCG, which is currently on display at the China National Exhibition Center.

The field of battery research is currently driven by the need to comprehend and optimize the performance of batteries at the cell level. This objective is supported by a growing number of complete-cell simulations, which are advancing through the development of new experimental techniques, modeling methods, and measurement tools. This review examines the fundamental principles of complete-cell simulation, covering the integration of multi-physics phenomena, the modeling of electrodes and electrolytes, and the analysis of electrochemical reactions. The discussion also explores the application of these simulations to various cell architectures, including cylindrical, prismatic, and pouch formats. Furthermore, the text addresses the challenges of validating these models using experimental data and highlights the potential of machine learning to streamline the development of complete-cell simulations.

Visual object search involves locating a target based on a query image, a task that is inherently complex due to the need for visual perception, scene comprehension, and action planning. While current research predominantly focuses on static settings, real-world applications require mobile agents to navigate dynamic environments. This paper introduces a Mobile Multi-View Visual Object Search (MMVOS) framework designed for mobile agents to retrieve target objects from various perspectives. The proposed method integrates a multi-view encoder with a deep reinforcement learning-based planner to generate effective search trajectories. Specifically, the encoder utilizes a view selection strategy to identify the most informative camera angle, while the planner employs a graph neural network to construct a view graph and determine the optimal sequence of viewpoints for searching. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches.

This study introduces a hyperdimensional computing (HDC) framework designed to enhance the recognition of seizure events within EEG recordings. The methodology integrates three core HDC strategies: (1) encoding input data into high-dimensional vectors, (2) executing vector operations to generate representations that capture data patterns, and (3) performing binding and hashing-based learning to synthesize and store knowledge. The resulting architecture is evaluated against several baseline models, including standard machine learning approaches and deep learning methods. The findings demonstrate that the proposed HDC approach surpasses these benchmarks in both accuracy and robustness, specifically in detecting seizures.

Gravitational wave (GW) standard sirens offer a novel method for determining cosmological parameters, particularly the Hubble constant ($H_0$). This study examines the potential of GW standard sirens to constrain $H_0$ using data from the Deci-hertz Observatory (DHO). We calculate the GW event detection rate within the DHO band, accounting for the merger rates of binary black holes (BBH) and binary neutron stars (BBNs). We then forecast the precision of $H_0$ measurements achievable with DHO, analyzing how these constraints vary with different BBH and BBN merger rates, as well as with varying numbers of electromagnetic (EM) counterparts. Our findings indicate that GW standard sirens from the DHO band can constrain $H_0$ with a precision of approximately 10% for BBH events and 20% for BBN events, assuming a merger rate of $10^{-3} \text{ Mpc}^{-3} \text{ yr}^{-1}$ for both populations and no EM counterparts. We further demonstrate that increasing the number of EM counterparts significantly enhances the precision of $H_0$ measurements derived from BBN standard sirens.

This paper presents Executive Function, a new algorithm designed to optimize the management of variable scopes in SQL queries. It employs a hybrid methodology that combines a rule-based component for handling straightforward cases with a learning component tailored to complex scenarios. The system's learning phase relies on hindsight summarization, which analyzes the outcomes of previous attempts to identify and apply effective strategies. By utilizing this approach, Executive Function effectively manages the resampling and renaming of instances within SQL queries. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that the proposed method surpasses existing state-of-the-art techniques in performance.

The integration of artificial intelligence in healthcare has gained significant traction, yet the potential for algorithms to perpetuate biases remains underexplored. This study examines bias within medical image collections by examining the link between demographic characteristics and image content. We introduce a novel methodology for identifying intrinsic biases inherent in these data sets, along with a new metric designed to quantify such bias. Our analysis reveals substantial disparities in the representation of various groups across different medical imaging datasets. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these intrinsic biases can negatively impact the performance of machine learning models trained on them.

The surge in deep neural network capabilities has driven a significant focus on enhancing their robustness against noise. While recent research has primarily concentrated on noise within the label space, a substantial amount of error also originates from the feature space, often due to data augmentation or adversarial attacks. To address this, we introduce the Proxy-Ancor Loss (PACL), a new metric learning approach designed for training noisy models. PACL utilizes two distinct auxiliary metrics: a "feature proxy" that captures the global semantic essence of the data and an "anchor proxy" that represents the specific semantic meaning of individual samples. PACL is engineered to be computationally efficient, requiring no additional memory overhead and supporting batch sizes of any magnitude. Furthermore, it is versatile enough to be integrated with various existing loss functions, such as Cross Entropy, Triplet Loss, and Contrastive Loss. Extensive testing on the CIFAR-10 and ImageNet datasets confirms that PACL significantly improves model robustness against label noise, achieving a 1.5% increase in accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods.

This work investigates the integrable structure of the SO(5) symmetry within the context of doped Mott insulators. We demonstrate that the SO(5) symmetry encompasses a unified framework for spin, charge, and pseudogap order parameters, and we establish a specific form for the SO(5) symmetric superconducting order parameter. Furthermore, we analyze the topological properties of the SO(5) order parameter, identifying a non-trivial topological phase in the vicinity of the phase transition. We also examine the SO(5) symmetry breaking and its associated consequences. Finally, we discuss the potential experimental signatures of the SO(5) symmetry in high-temperature superconductors.

The position is determined by analyzing the output signal distribution across the SiPM channels. Theoretical calculations indicate that a 4x4 SiPM configuration can achieve a spatial resolution of 100 μm. This paper examines the partial genera $\gamma_k(A)$ of a commutative Noetherian ring $A$, defined as $\dim_{\mathrm{K}}\mathrm{K}(A)\otimes_{\mathrm{K}}\mathrm{K}(M_k)$, where $M_k$ represents the $k$-th syzygy module of a finite $A$-module $M$ and $\mathrm{K}$ denotes the field of fractions of $K$. We demonstrate that for any commutative Noetherian ring $A$ and finite $A$-module $M$, the partial genera $\gamma_k(A)$ form a monotonically decreasing sequence of non-negative rational numbers. Furthermore, we establish that $\gamma_k(A)=0$ for all $k\geq 0$ if and only if $A$ is Cohen-Macaulay. We also derive the relationship between $\gamma_k(A)$ and the depth of $M$ and prove that $\gamma_k(M)$ remains constant for $k\geq \mathrm{depth}(M)$. Additionally, we show that $\gamma_k(M)$ is bounded above by $\mathrm{pd}_A(M)-k+1$ for $k\leq \mathrm{pd}_A(M)$. Finally, we provide a formula for $\gamma_k(A)$ in terms of the local cohomology modules of $A$.

This study presents the first nuclear forward scattering (NFS) measurements of the Bi$_5$FeTi$_3$O$_{15}$ compound under high pressure, revealing a significant pressure-induced enhancement in the magnetic ordering temperature. This increase is attributed to the suppression of the antiferromagnetic order by non-magnetic Bi$^{3+}$ ions, which disrupts the Fe and Ti magnetic layers. The results underscore the critical role of the non-magnetic Bi sublattice in governing the magnetic behavior of this five-layered Aurivillius phase.

This study introduces a Bayesian framework for evaluating and ranking trading algorithms, with a specific focus on assessing trading expenses. The methodology is applied to a portfolio selection problem, where the chosen portfolio maximizes the Sharpe ratio.

We introduce a class of optomechanical add-drop devices designed to regulate the transmission and output frequencies of light. These devices utilize a ring resonator equipped with two movable mirrors, which can be positioned to either block or create an aperture in the side-coupled waveguide. By adjusting the mirror gaps, the system allows for the tunability of the resonator's quality factor, the transmission ratio, and the resonance frequency. Our analysis demonstrates that the mirrors' movable nature enables complete control over the transmission spectrum and the resonance frequency. Furthermore, we investigate the interaction between the movable mirrors and the resonator's mechanical mode, which can be excited by the optical field.

Health strategies are frequently disseminated through various media, including print, television, and radio. However, assessing the effectiveness of these initiatives remains difficult due to the dispersed nature of the target demographic and the lack of cooperation among them. This paper introduces a novel approach to evaluate such health programs by employing image search engines to locate visual materials created specifically for the campaign. We outline a methodology for assessing these materials, ranging from their physical condition to their contextual setting. Subsequently, we demonstrate how to utilize this data to determine whether a strategy has successfully reached its intended audience.

This paper introduces a new end-to-end lossless compression framework for GPU-accelerated image compression, built upon a novel encoder-decoder architecture. The system employs a two-stage process: first, a quantization stage transforms images into 16-bit integers, followed by a compression stage that reduces these integers into bitstreams. We present two distinct quantization methods: one utilizing a quantization table and the other using a quantization network. The latter is trained via a loss function to minimize the bitstream size of the resulting compressed data. Furthermore, we propose a new lossless compression method that leverages the encoder-decoder architecture to generate bitstreams. The proposed framework is evaluated against state-of-the-art methods on the LKBD dataset, demonstrating superior performance in terms of compression ratio. Additionally, we compare our method with existing state-of-the-art methods on the LKBD dataset, showing that our method is more efficient in terms of compression ratio. This study examines the decays $B^{+} \to D_s^{+}K^{+}K^{-}$ and $B^{+} \to D_s^{+}\phi$ using data from the BESIII detector collected at the $\psi(3770)$ resonance, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 1.0 fb$^{-1}$. No significant evidence for the three-body decay mode is found; consequently, a 90% confidence level upper limit of $\mathcal{B}(B^{+} \to D_s^{+}K^{+}K^{-}) < 1.0 \times 10^{-4}$ is established. Additionally, the two-body decay $B^{+} \to D_s^{+}\phi$ is investigated via the $B^{+} \to D_s^{+}\phi \to D_s^{+}\pi^{+}\pi^{-}$ process. The analysis reveals a signal of 11.1 $\pm$ 2.0 (stat.) $\pm$ 0.7 (syst.) events, yielding a branching fraction of $\mathcal{B}(B^{+} \to D_s^{+}\phi) = (1.1 \pm 0.2 \pm 0.1) \times 10^{-5}$.

The Ideal Transport (IT) framework is a potent tool for analyzing and visualizing the evolution of vector fields, including atmospheric and oceanic currents. However, its standard formulation is highly sensitive to anomalous data points, which can severely distort derived insights. This paper introduces a straightforward and effective strategy for constructing anomaly-resilient IT models. Our findings demonstrate that this robust approach significantly mitigates the impact of outliers on both the computational efficiency and accuracy of atmospheric and oceanic flow analyses.

This paper introduces a framework for enabling AI agents to learn to collaborate effectively with humans and other AI teammates by integrating human decision-making models with reinforcement learning. We specifically address scenarios where an agent must infer a human's preference model from observed interactions and then align its behavior to ensure compatibility with those preferences. We present a novel, efficient algorithm that learns the human's choice model alongside a complementary set of policy constraints, allowing the agent to generate trajectories that fit within these limits. We demonstrate that our approach can successfully learn to coordinate with both human and AI partners in a cooperative driving task, successfully inferring their respective preferences and adapting its strategy to foster cooperation.

This paper examines the robustness of supersymmetry (SUSY) against quantum corrections. We demonstrate that the SUSY Ward identities connecting renormalization group (RG) functions are inherently independent of regularization methods. Furthermore, we show that SUSY ensures the renormalizability of any theory possessing such symmetry. Finally, we derive a specific identity relating the beta function for the anomalous dimension of a conserved current to the coefficient of its corresponding Wess-Zumino term.

Visualization research has frequently concentrated on the nature of data and visual encodings, often neglecting the distinct cognitive and perceptual attributes of the viewers. This study investigates how a viewer's background knowledge and expertise influence their performance on visualization tasks. We conducted a study involving 120 participants recruited from three distinct fields: computer science, engineering, and the humanities. Participants completed three separate tasks designed to assess their spatial reasoning abilities, followed by a series of interactive scatter plot activities intended to evaluate how these factors impact viewer performance on task outcomes. The findings reveal that while participants' expertise levels significantly correlated with higher scores on the spatial reasoning assessments, this expertise did not translate into superior performance on the actual visualization tasks. Consequently, the results indicate that task success is primarily dictated by the specific nature of the data and visualizations employed, rather than the viewers' disciplinary expertise.

We introduce a new form of proof for the validity of universal quantifiers in clause sets, which can be defined as the failure of induction. This form of induction bears a resemblance to Kowalski and Overbeek's inductive definition of logic programs, with the key distinction that it applies to any collection of clauses rather than just those in a program. This form of induction necessitates the existence of a specific type of clause set loop, known as a universal loop, to confirm the validity of a given clause set.

We introduce a neural network designed to extract subgraphs from larger graphs, utilizing a two-stage process. First, a segmentation model identifies the specific nodes that constitute a target subgraph. Second, an alignment model maps the target to the source structure, aligning unlabelled nodes from source subgraphs with those of the target based on their topological relationships. We evaluate the performance of this proposed framework against the standard approach of subgraph matching.

This study introduces a novel training methodology for feedforward neural networks designed to model transient dynamics. The approach leverages concepts from natural language processing, specifically the utilization of n-grams and the generation of diverse sentence structures. The algorithm is validated on a chaotic system—a pendulum with an oscillating base—where it successfully reconstructs the system's behavior.

This study examines the design of division algorithms for power distribution networks where each node possesses a specific demand. We propose a new framework that ensures fairness among nodes by defining the concept of equitable allocation. We present two algorithms, EquiFlow and EquiFlow+, which are designed to achieve this equitable distribution. The EquiFlow algorithm is grounded in the principles of the flow-based method known as the "water-filling algorithm," whereas EquiFlow+ utilizes a gradient descent approach. We have demonstrated that the EquiFlow algorithm is capable of converging to an equitable allocation within a finite number of iterations. Additionally, we have established that the EquiFlow+ algorithm is guaranteed to converge to an equitable allocation. We have also analyzed the computational complexity of both proposed algorithms. Furthermore, we have conducted numerical experiments to evaluate the performance of these algorithms.

Resolving coreference is a vital natural language processing task that links pronouns and descriptive noun phrases to their specific referents within a text. While recent advancements have significantly improved coreference resolution capabilities, most existing research focuses on general domains, neglecting the specific challenges posed by controversial political events. This study introduces the "Coref-Occ" dataset, a collection of news articles from the 2016 U.S. Presidential Election annotated with occurrences coreferenced. We demonstrate that standard coreference models struggle to accurately identify occurrences within these texts, largely due to the presence of ambiguity. To address this, we developed a new evaluation metric called "Coref-Occ F1," which measures the precision of linking occurrences to their correct antecedents. Our analysis reveals that ambiguous contexts are the primary barrier to resolving occurrence references in controversial political news.

This paper examines knapsack problems with negative item coefficients, referred to as complementarity knapsack problems (CKP). It introduces the concept of a facet as a specific solution set derived from a particular problem instance. The study establishes a novel classification system for these problem facets, offering a systematic approach to analyzing and comprehending the solution sets inherent to CKP instances.

We demonstrate that within the context of the Weinberg symmetry group, massive spin-$j$ fields are defined by two parameters exclusively, which correspond to helicity. This finding emerges from the observation that a massive spin-$j$ representation is constituted by the direct sum of $2j+1$ distinct helicity representations.

This study establishes a framework for group actions on nonlinear maps, termed *transversal groups*, and outlines a methodology to define such actions for specific map classes. We present a definition of *Favard measure* utilizing transversal groups to extend the concept of Favard length, alongside a characterization of this expansion. Furthermore, we demonstrate that when applied to complex polynomials, our proposed generalization retains the essential properties inherent to Favard length.

This study presents a direct, black-box reinforcement learning approach that requires minimal demonstration data and guarantees safety. The method draws inspiration from control-theoretic strategies for robotic motion planning, specifically resilient tube model predictive control (MPC). This underlying control principle ensures adherence to safety constraints by planning within a "resilient tube"—a safety envelope that remains invariant under the system's dynamics. By integrating this concept into a reinforcement learning framework, we define a task-specific reward function that incentivizes the agent to stay within the tube. We validate the efficacy of this strategy through simulations on a quadruped robot tasked with navigating a hazardous environment.

The third-order Hall effect, a nonlinear response to electric and magnetic fields, has been extensively investigated in recent years. In this study, we present a generalized semiclassical framework for calculating third-order Hall conductivity, which accommodates arbitrary band structures. Our analysis reveals that this conductivity can emerge as an inherent property of time-reversal-inversion symmetric systems, driven by the Berry curvature of the energy third derivatives. This contribution is quantified by a momentum-space integral of a Berry curvature form, which exhibits a topological character. We demonstrate that this term is quantized in systems with inversion symmetry, contingent upon the presence of band inversion. Furthermore, we establish a connection between this intrinsic Hall conductivity and the Berry curvature of the energy third derivatives, which can be expressed as a Berry curvature current. Finally, we provide a theoretical estimate of the magnitude of the third-order Hall conductivity arising from this intrinsic mechanism.

Software reverse engineering (SRE) is a critical field that involves analyzing the internal workings of a program without access to its source code. A primary objective within SRE is to compare different program implementations to identify their similarities and differences. While numerous tools exist for reverse engineering individual programs, few are designed specifically to perform comparative analysis across multiple programs. This paper introduces a scalable method for comparing call graphs, a fundamental component of reverse engineering. Our approach employs a novel algorithm that generates a compact, scalable representation of call graphs, which can then be compared using established techniques. We have implemented this method in a practical tool and evaluated its performance on call graphs derived from both synthetic and real-world programs.

The "One Billion Word Standard" serves as a widely accepted benchmark for evaluating information-theoretic data compression. This article critiques the standard by arguing that it incentivizes submitters to create overly specific encodings for their datasets, thereby introducing inherent biases. We demonstrate that these biases are so severe that they render the resulting compression scores unreliable for comparing information density across different datasets.

We report the detection of quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in microwave emissions from a current layer formed during a flare, utilizing data from the Nobeyama Radioheliograph (NHR) and the Nobeyama 45-m telescope. These emissions were observed in a region of the flare's core where the microwave source was spatially resolved, revealing a complex structure of multiple loops. The observed QPOs exhibited a period of approximately 100 seconds, with a spatial extent of about 10,000 km. This scale is consistent with the size of the magnetic reconnection region, suggesting that the reconnection process is occurring within a quasi-periodic state.

Industrial quality evaluation is a critical component of the manufacturing sector, where defects in products can result in significant financial losses. Consequently, there is a pressing need to develop a robust quality inspection system capable of detecting anomalies in real-time. This paper introduces a novel multi-scale anomaly identification technique designed for industrial quality evaluation. The proposed method employs a multi-scale framework to capture both local and global features, utilizing a deep learning architecture to model normal behavior and pinpoint deviations. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach outperforms current state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.

This paper investigates the dispersion-generalized Kadomtsev-Petviashvili I (KP-I) equation, defined as
$$
\partial_t u + \partial_x^k u u + u_{xxx} + u_{xyy} = 0, \quad k \geq 3,
$$
where $u$ represents the $k$-th order dispersion. We demonstrate local well-posedness within the irregular Sobolev space $H^s(\mathbb{T}^2)$ for parameters satisfying $s \in \left[\frac{3-k}{2}, \frac{3-k}{2} + \frac{1}{k}\right)$.

This study explores the phenomenon of Kramers degeneracy within the context of open quantum systems, specifically focusing on systems governed by non-Hermitian Hamiltonians. We demonstrate that degeneracy can be violated in such environments, even when the Hamiltonian maintains PT symmetry. Furthermore, we examine degeneracy breaches resulting from the interaction between a quantum system and its environment, showing that these interactions can induce particle number parity shifts in the spectrum. We also reveal that the resulting spectrum may exhibit parity time (PT) symmetry breaking, which manifests as a breach of Kramers degeneracy. Consequently, our findings suggest that PT symmetry breaking can be achieved in open quantum systems without the need to break spatial inversion symmetry.

This study introduces a new approach for anticipating future Channel State Information (CSI) responses in highly mobile Massive MIMO networks. By leveraging the inherent sparsity of the channel's time-domain representation, we develop a sparse deep autoencoder (SDAE) capable of forecasting subsequent channel states. The SDAE is trained using historical CSI data to learn the underlying channel dynamics, enabling it to predict future responses with high accuracy. Simulation outcomes demonstrate that this proposed method significantly outperforms existing solutions in terms of performance.

This work examines the scaling limit of rescaled Szeg\H{o} kernels on a class of pseudoconvex manifolds known as Grauert cylinders. These manifolds are characterized by the existence of an infinite sequence of holomorphic self-mappings that shrink the manifold toward a single point. We demonstrate that the rescaled Szeg\H{o} kernels converge to the product of the infinite Gaussian hermitian universal kernel and the Bergman projection associated with the base \mathbb{C}^n. This finding extends previous results by Demaille and Zhang, who established a similar convergence for domains with an explicit automorphism group action.

The Inverse Line Chart Creation (ILCC) problem involves deriving a set of matrices from a known line chart. This challenge was initially introduced by Roussopoulos in 1993, who proposed a solution based on the Matrix Relocation (MR) technique. Subsequently, in 2017, the MARINLINGA group introduced an improved algorithm, MARINLINGA, which operates by executing the MR process followed by post-processing steps to ensure all matrices adhere to the required constraints. This paper evaluates the performance of the MARINLINGA technique against the original Roussopoulos method, demonstrating that MARINLINGA outperforms the earlier approach in both time and space efficiency.
The article demonstrates that all right-leaning modules, as conjectured by Lee and Lee in the context of the module theory, are topologically equivalent.

Java applications typically rely on external libraries, which can be compromised by bugs or security flaws. Although developers frequently update these dependencies to rectify such issues, the impact of these fixes on the broader ecosystem remains unclear. This study examines the consequences of dependency updates across 1,000 Java projects tracked over a six-year span. Our analysis reveals that 70% of these projects initiated at least one update, with 10% initiating more than 50 updates.
